title: Fecal microbiota transplantation accelerates clearance of carbapenemase-producing Enterobacterales intestinal carriage: influence of recipient gut microbiome ecology.
abstract: Background Persistent intestinal carbapenemase-producing Enterobacterales (CPE) carriage challenges infection prevention and antimicrobial stewardship. We evaluated fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) for decolonization and response-associated recipient microbiome features. Methods This prospective cohort study assessed intestinal CPE clearance in 131 adult carriers (68 receiving FMT; 63 under observation). Responders achieved clearance, defined as three consecutive negative rectal surveillance cultures for CPE, obtained at 3-day intervals within 1 month after FMT. Following least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO)-based covariate selection, Cox proportional hazards models estimated associations between FMT and time to successful decolonization within prespecified 0-30-day and 0-90-day windows. A longitudinal metagenomic subcohort of 21 FMT recipients (102 fecal samples) underwent shotgun sequencing to characterize taxonomic composition, microbial network organization, functional pathways, antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs), and donor engraftment. Results After LASSO-based covariate selection, FMT was associated with faster CPE clearance than observation at 1 month (hazard ratio, 4.02; 95% confidence interval, 1.84-8.79), with effects sustained at 3 months. Responders showed relatively preserved baseline microbial network organization and enrichment of taxa annotated with arginine-related pathway features, suggesting metabolic relevance to microbial niche competition. After FMT, responders had greater engraftment of donor-associated taxa and donor-like ecological reassembly, with reduced Klebsiella pneumoniae dominance and ARG abundance. Conclusions FMT may accelerate intestinal decolonization in CPE carriers; response variability was associated with recipient gut-microbiome ecology, suggesting microbiome-guided patient selection could optimize microbiota-based strategies.
authors: Lee I, Suk KT, Park JY, Yong D, Kim DJ, Kim BS, Lee SS.
screening_reason: Focuses on fecal microbiota transplantation and recipient gut microbiome ecology during intestinal CPE decolonization.
summary_ja: カルバペネマーゼ産生腸内細菌目細菌（CPE）の腸内保有者131名を対象に、糞便微生物移植（FMT）による脱定着効果を検討した前瞻的コホート研究である。FMT群は観察群と比較して1か月および3か月時点でのCPEクリアランスが有意に促進された。ショットガンメタゲノム解析の結果、治療反応者ではベースライン時の細菌ネットワーク構造が維持されており、アルギニン関連代謝経路の富集が見られた。FMT後、反応者ではドナー由来の菌の生着と生態系再構築が進行し、薬剤耐性遺伝子の存在量が減少した。
summary_en: A prospective cohort study evaluated the efficacy of fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) for clearing intestinal carbapenemase-producing Enterobacterales carriage in adults. FMT significantly accelerated CPE clearance compared with observation over 1-month and 3-month follow-up windows. Metagenomic analysis revealed that clinical response was associated with recipient baseline gut microbiome ecology and enhanced donor strain engraftment.
key_finding_ja: FMTはCPE腸内保有者の除菌を加速させ、その治療反応性は受容者のベースライン時の腸内細菌叢生態系と関連していた。
why_it_matters_ja: 腸内細菌叢の生態学的特徴に基づく患者選定が、多剤耐性菌の脱定着を目的としたマイクロバイオーム療法の最適化に役立つ可能性がある。

title: VlPAG/DRN Microglia Drive Neuropathic Pain-Induced Depression via a Defined Neuroimmune Axis.
abstract: Neuropathic pain is frequently comorbid with anxiety and depression, yet the mechanisms linking immune signaling to affective brain circuits remain poorly understood. Here, we identify a neuroimmune circuit in which peripheral nerve injury activates microglia in the midbrain ventrolateral periaqueductal gray/dorsal raphe (vlPAG/DRN), triggering an NLRP3-IL-1β-dependent inflammatory cascade. Direct optogenetic or chemogenetic activation of vlPAG/DRN microglia is sufficient to drive negative affective behaviors. We show that local VGLUT2 + glutamatergic neurons (vlPAG/DRN Glu ) are the principal IL-1R1-expressing targets; IL-1β activates these neurons to drive anxiety- and depression-like states. Conversely, microglia-specific Nlrp3 deletion or local IL-1R1 blockade prevents neuropathic pain-induced affective deficits. Furthermore, circuit mapping and functional manipulation reveal an excitatory vlPAG/DRN Glu to the bed nucleus of the stria terminalis (BNST GABA ) pathway that is both sufficient to induce and required to maintain the affective component of neuropathic pain. Together, our findings delineate a microglia-vlPAG/DRN Glu -BNST GABA axis that translates peripheral injury into maladaptive emotional states, revealing a discrete neuroimmune circuit substrate for mood comorbidity in chronic pain.
authors: Yang J, Tang BJ, Li JY, Xie SL, Duan S, Chen J, Zhu S, Xu ZZ.
screening_reason: Identifies a central midbrain microglial neuroimmune circuit driving neuropathic pain-induced depression.
summary_ja: 末梢神経障害に伴う不安や抑うつにおける神経免疫応答の解明を目的とした研究である。中脳腹外側頭蓋底灰白質/背側縫線核（vlPAG/DRN）のミクログリアがNLRP3-IL-1β炎症カスケードを活性化することを示した。このIL-1β応答によりVGLUT2陽性グルタミン酸作動性神経（vlPAG/DRN Glu）が刺激され、情動障害様行動が誘発される。さらにvlPAG/DRN Gluから界床核（BNST GABA）への興奮性神経回路がこの感情障害の維持に必要かつ十分であることを明らかにした。
summary_en: This study investigated the neuroimmune circuit underlying neuropathic pain-induced anxiety and depression. Peripheral nerve injury activates microglia in the vlPAG/DRN to trigger an NLRP3-IL-1β inflammatory cascade that excites local glutamatergic neurons. Furthermore, an excitatory pathway from vlPAG/DRN glutamatergic neurons to the bed nucleus of the stria terminalis is required and sufficient to maintain these affective deficits.
key_finding_ja: 末梢神経障害は中脳のミクログリアにおけるNLRP3-IL-1βカスケードと特定の神経回路を介して抑うつや不安行動を誘導する。
why_it_matters_ja: 神経障害性痛みに伴う感情障害の神経免疫メカニズムを解明したことで、新規治療標的の開発に寄与する可能性がある。

title: The genesis of cutaneous neurogenic inflammation is a multi-step process requiring dendritic cell aggregation.
abstract: Cutaneous inflammation involving neuroimmune interactions can be initiated by both neurons and immune cells, making it complicated to parse the mechanisms of neurogenic inflammation. Optogenetic activation of Trpv1-expressing nociceptors drives type-17 inflammation in the absence of other inflammatory triggers. We found that two rounds of nociceptor activation were required for Il23a expression and maximal expression of Il1b and Il6, key drivers of type-17 inflammation. The first round of nociceptor activation triggered transient type 2 dendritic cell (DC2) aggregation that required substance P-Mrgprb2-dependent mast cell activation and mast cell-derived chemokine CCL2. Spatial transcriptomic analysis revealed that DC aggregation allowed the second nociceptor stimulation to efficiently activate DCs via the neuropeptide calcitonin gene-related peptide α (CGRPα). Thus, early neurogenic inflammation is a two-step process: substance P induces Mrgprb2-dependent mast cell activation and formation of DC aggregates that allow for efficient subsequent CGRPα-mediated DC activation. These data reveal a multi-cell, dynamic mechanism underlying neurogenic inflammation.
authors: Chen CS, Gillis JE, Cohen JA, Glathar AR, Chen Y, Weiss ES, McKendrick LM, Bacon CO, Smith CJ, Spencer NJ, Chiu IM, Davis BM, Sumpter TL, Cillo AR, Poholek AC, Kaplan DH.
screening_reason: Detailed mechanistic study of cutaneous neurogenic inflammation driven by nociceptor, mast cell, and dendritic cell neuroimmune interactions.
summary_ja: 光遺伝学的なTrpv1発現傷害受容体の刺激による皮膚の神経性炎症の発症メカニズムを検証した。2段階の受容体刺激がIl23aなどの17型炎症因子の発現誘導に必須であることを発見した。初回の刺激はサブスタンスP-Mrgprb2依存的なマスト細胞の活性化とケモカインCCL2を介して2型樹状細胞（DC2）の集合を誘導した。このDC2集合体形成により、2回目の刺激で放出されるCGRPαペプチドを介してDCが効率的に活性化される多段階プロセスが明らかになった。
summary_en: The authors demonstrated that cutaneous neurogenic inflammation induced by optogenetic Trpv1 nociceptor activation is a multi-step process requiring two rounds of stimulation. The initial activation triggered substance P- and CCL2-dependent dendritic cell (DC2) aggregation via mast cells. This spatial aggregation allowed subsequent CGRPα release during the second stimulation to efficiently activate DCs and drive type-17 inflammation.
key_finding_ja: 皮膚の神経性炎症の成立には、サブスタンスPによるマスト細胞・樹状細胞集合の形成と、それに続くCGRPαによる樹状細胞の活性化という2段階の細胞間相互作用が必要であることが判明した。
why_it_matters_ja: 神経と免疫細胞の動的な多段階相互作用の解明は、神経性皮膚炎症性疾患の制御に向けた新たな治療戦略の提案につながる可能性がある。

title: Resistome and microbiome-immune interactions in an Eastern European population with high antibiotic use.
abstract: The gut microbiome influences host health, affecting gastrointestinal, metabolic, immune, cardiovascular, and neurological functions. A balanced microbiome is associated with favorable health outcomes. However, excessive antibiotic use and dietary habits can disrupt this ecosystem, leading to dysbiosis and affecting body homeostasis. This first comprehensive metagenomic analysis of the gut microbiome in a healthy Romanian cohort, a population underrepresented in microbiome studies and characterized by high antibiotic consumption, addresses a gap in current microbiome research. We report an enrichment of Enterobacteriaceae although overall composition is more comparable to other European than non-European cohorts. Community configurations align with established enterotype patterns, and our analysis provides insight into their relationship with within-phylum diversity. The analysis of antimicrobial resistance provides insight into the prevalence of resistance genes within this reservoir. We specifically report the presence of cfr(E ), a Clostridioides difficile gene, and tet(X5 ), a variant from the ubiquitous tet family, genes not previously reported in healthy European populations. Integration with data from the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control links the overall prevalence of resistance genes in this reservoir to antibiotic classes with higher community consumption in this population, notably beta-lactams and quinolones, highlighting potential targets for antibiotic stewardship programs. Finally, we investigate the relationship between the microbial profile and the systemic immune responses, inferred from correlations with in vitro cytokine production. Notably, we identify potential immune-priming roles for Collinsella , Flavonifractor, and Bifidobacterium species.IMPORTANCEThis first comprehensive study of the healthy gut microbiome in a Romanian cohort addresses a gap in current microbiome research, dominated by data sets from a limited number of regions. It sets a baseline for the microbiome and resistome composition of this population, and, while definitions of "healthy" microbiomes, or baseline resistomes, remain lacking, such study helps contextualize future studies and support the monitoring of dynamics. The Enterobacteriaceae abundance suggests a microbiome composition potentially influenced by antimicrobial consumption, a relevant pattern in a region with a high burden of nosocomial infections. In addition, the prevalence of antimicrobial resistance genes and the concordance with commonly used antibiotics in the community reinforce the need to address antibiotic use in public health strategies. Although gut microbiome-immunity relationships remain incompletely understood, our findings support a role for microbiome composition in immune-related traits and provide a valuable resource for future studies.
authors: Mirăuță B, Riza A-L, Streata I, Pirvu A, Dorobantu S, Dragos A, Surleac M, Netea MG.
screening_reason: Metagenomic study focused directly on human gut microbiome composition and microbiome-host immune interactions.
summary_ja: 抗菌薬消費量の多いルーマニアの健常成人コホートを対象に、腸内細菌叢およびレジストームの包括的なメタゲノム解析を実施した。全体的な構成は欧州の他コホートと類似していたが、エンテロバクテリア科の濃縮が認められた。また、健常欧州コホートで未報告であったcfr(E)やtet(X5)などの薬剤耐性遺伝子が検出され、地域でのβ-ラクタム系やキノロン系の消費量と関連していた。さらに、CollinsellaやBifidobacteriumなどの特定菌株が体外でのサイトカイン産生と相関し、全身性免疫のプライミングに関与する可能性が示された。
summary_en: A comprehensive metagenomic analysis of a healthy Romanian cohort with high antibiotic consumption revealed enriched Enterobacteriaceae and identified previously unreported antimicrobial resistance genes such as cfr(E) and tet(X5). The resistome profile mirrored the high community use of beta-lactams and quinolones. Additionally, specific gut microbes correlated with in vitro cytokine production, suggesting microbiome-mediated immune priming.
key_finding_ja: 抗菌薬使用量の多いルーマニア健康コホートにおいて、特徴的な薬剤耐性遺伝子の存在と微生物叢による免疫応答への影響が示された。
why_it_matters_ja: 地域固有の抗菌薬消費と腸内細菌叢・レジストームおよび免疫応答の関係を把握することは、将来の抗菌薬適正使用プログラムの策定に役立つ可能性がある。

title: Protein persulfidation emerges as a conserved component of the redox response to DNA damage.
abstract: Genotoxic stress is frequently accompanied by alterations in cellular redox homeostasis; however, the mechanisms linking redox regulation to the DNA damage response (DDR) remain incompletely understood. Here, we investigated the early redox response to DNA damage induced by methyl methanesulfonate (MMS) in Saccharomyces cerevisiae, focusing on cysteine oxidative post-translational modifications (PTM). We show that activation of the DNA damage response is accompanied by rapid redox changes that occur in the absence of a generalized oxidative stress response. MMS exposure promotes selective remodeling of cysteine oxidative modifications, characterized by decreased free thiols, robust induction of protein persulfidation, and comparatively modest changes in sulfenylation. These alterations are accompanied by increased intracellular hydrogen sulfide levels, supporting the involvement of reactive sulfur species in the cellular response to DNA damage. Proteome-wide analyses revealed that cysteine oxidative modifications preferentially target proteins involved in central metabolism, nucleotide biosynthesis, and genome maintenance. Consistent with these observations, MMS-induced genotoxic stress promotes metabolic adaptation characterized by increased mitochondrial respiration, elevated ATP production, and mitochondrial morphological remodeling, linking bioenergetic adaptation to redox regulation. Importantly, perturbation of intracellular redox balance using N-acetylcysteine compromises survival under DNA-damaging conditions, supporting a functional role for redox signaling during the DDR. Finally, MMS treatment also induces protein persulfidation in mammalian cells. Moreover, exposure to etoposide, a mechanistically distinct genotoxic agent that induces DNA double-strand breaks through topoisomerase II inhibition, showed a similar trend, suggesting that protein persulfidation may not be restricted to alkylation-induced DNA damage. Together our findings identify protein persulfidation as a prominent component of the redox response to DNA damage and provide new insight into the functional interplay between mitochondrial metabolism, cysteine-based redox regulation, and genome maintenance.
authors: Ramírez-Robles D, Espinoza-Simón E, López-Miranda M, Juárez-Meléndez K, Nieto-Zaragoza E, Torres-Marcial K, Ríos-Castro E, Filipovic M, Torres-Quiroz F.
screening_reason: Directly focuses on protein persulfidation, reactive sulfur species, and cysteine oxidative post-translational modifications in response to DNA damage.
category_ja: 超硫黄分子・超硫黄修飾
summary_ja: 本研究では、MMS誘導性のDNA損傷に対する酵母および哺乳類細胞の早期酸化還元応答を解析した。ゲノムストレス下において遊離チオールの減少と共にタンパク質のペルスルフィド化が著しく誘導され、硫化水素レベルの上昇が観察された。ペルスルフィド化修飾は中心代謝、塩基合成、ゲノム維持に関わるタンパク質に優先的に生じ、ミトコンドリア呼吸やATP産生の増加を伴う代謝適合が引き起こされた。N-アセチルシステインによる酸化還元バランスの攪乱は生存率を低下させ、ペルスルフィド化がDDRにおける保存された重要な要素であることが示された。
summary_en: This study investigated the redox response to genotoxic stress in yeast and mammalian cells, revealing a rapid induction of protein persulfidation following DNA damage. Cysteine oxidative modifications preferentially targeted proteins involved in metabolism, nucleotide synthesis, and genome maintenance, accompanied by enhanced mitochondrial respiration. Disruption of redox balance impaired cell survival, establishing protein persulfidation as a conserved component of the DNA damage response.
key_finding_ja: DNA損傷応答においてタンパク質のペルスルフィド化が迅速かつ選択的に誘導され、ミトコンドリア代謝適合と細胞生存に寄与することが見出された。
why_it_matters_ja: 超硫黄分子修飾がDNA損傷応答および代謝制御において果たす役割の解明は、ゲノム安定性と酸化還元生物学の統合的理解につながる可能性がある。

title: Neuron-Derived Neuroinflammation in Neurodegenerative Diseases: Mechanisms and Intervention Prospects.
abstract: Neurodegenerative diseases represent a major global public health challenge, imposing substantial societal and economic burdens. Their complex pathogenesis and limited therapeutic options underscore an urgent need for new paradigms. Emerging evidence indicates that dysregulation of the brain's immune microenvironment is a critical driver of disease progression. Conventional wisdom posits that peripheral immune cells and central glial cells serve as the primary initiators of neuroimmune responses, whereas neurons are regarded merely as passive recipients of inflammatory damage. Emerging evidence suggests that upon receiving pathological signals in the central nervous system, neurons may become more vulnerable and participate in the onset of neuroimmune processes, positioning them as potential targets for early intervention in neurodegenerative diseases. This article systematically reviews the contribution of neuron-derived immune-inflammatory responses in neurodegenerative diseases and potential intervention strategies. We first outline the capacity of neurons to regulate neuroimmune responses and detail the underlying molecular mechanisms. Then we compare the specific mechanisms by which neurons with different susceptibility drive and amplify neuroinflammation in various neurodegenerative diseases such as alzheimer's disease, parkinson's disease, amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, vascular cognitive impairment, and transformed these mechanisms into intervention strategies targeting neurons,. This article aims to break through the traditional concept of passive neuronal damage, systematically integrate intervention strategies that shift from targeting peripheral immune and glial cells to regulating neuron-derived immunity, thereby providing a new theoretical framework for overcoming current clinical limitations and identifying effective therapeutic targets for the prevention and treatment of neurodegenerative diseases.
authors: Bu J, Nie X, Luo H, Wang J, Jiang D, Xu N, Zhuang P, Zhang Y, Yin Q.
screening_reason: Focuses directly on neuron-derived neuroinflammatory processes and neuroimmune mechanisms in central nervous system diseases.
summary_ja: 本総説は、神経変性疾患におけるニューロン由来の免疫・炎症応答の役割と治療的介入の可能性を体系的に論じている。従来、神経炎症はミクログリアやアストロサイト、末梢免疫細胞が主導し、ニューロンは受動的な障害対象と考えられていた。しかし近年の知見により、中枢神経系内の病理学的シグナルを受けたニューロン自体が神経免疫プロセスを駆動し、炎症を増幅させることが示されている。著者らはアルツハイマー病やパーキンソン病などにおけるニューロン特異的な免疫調節機構を整理し、ニューロンを標的とした新たな治療戦略を提唱している。
summary_en: This review systematically examines the emerging role of neuron-derived immune and inflammatory responses in neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer's and Parkinson's. Contrary to the traditional view of neurons as passive targets of inflammation, evidence suggests that neurons actively drive and amplify neuroinflammatory processes upon pathological stimuli. The authors summarize the cell-type-specific mechanisms of neuronal neuroimmunity and discuss therapeutic strategies targeting these neuronal pathways to prevent neurodegeneration.
key_finding_ja: ニューロンは単なる神経炎症の受動的な被害者ではなく、自ら免疫・炎症応答を駆動および増幅させる活性主体であることが明かされている。
why_it_matters_ja: 従来のグリア細胞や末梢免疫細胞中心の観点を転換し、ニューロン直接標的型の新たな神経変性疾患治療法の開発に寄与する可能性がある。

title: Microbiota-derived isovalerate ameliorates sex-specific gut barrier dysfunction in malnutrition.
abstract: Malnutrition increases intestinal permeability and the risk of sepsis, yet mechanisms underlying malnutrition-induced gut barrier dysfunction are poorly defined. Here, we aimed to determine how the gut microbiome and microbiota-derived metabolites influence intestinal barrier function in the malnourished host. We induced malnutrition in specific pathogen-free (SPF) and germ-free (GF) mice using a low-protein, low-fat diet. Colonic permeability was quantified in Ussing chambers and invasive bacteria were cultured from liver and spleen. Targeted metabolomics identified microbial metabolites depleted in malnutrition. Candidate metabolites were screened in human-derived colonoid monolayers and administered to malnourished mice to determine whether gut barrier dysfunction can be rescued. Malnutrition thinned the colonic mucus layer, increased gut barrier permeability, and facilitated bacterial translocation in male, but not female, SPF mice. Malnourished GF mice exhibited normal barrier function. In the malnourished intestine, a subset of microbial short-chain fatty acids, the branched-chain fatty acids (BCFAs), was depleted in SPF mice of both sexes. Treating human-derived colonoid monolayers with BCFAs, especially isovalerate, increased transepithelial electrical resistance and altered the expression of genes associated with epithelial junction complexes. In malnourished male SPF mice, either enemas with isovalerate or gavages with its branched-chain amino acid fermentation substrate, leucine, restored the localization of the integral membrane protein claudin-8 within the colonic crypt and reduced barrier permeability. Together, these findings identify BCFAs, including isovalerate, as microbiota-derived regulators of intestinal junction complexes and barrier integrity. We propose the branched-chain amino acid leucine as a microbiota-directed precision nutrition therapy that could target intestinal barrier dysfunction in malnutrition.
authors: Lynch LE, Soni KG, Spinler JK, Ambati CSR, Putluri N, Fowler SW, Conner ME, Nguyen-Phuc H, Zeng XL, Blutt SE, Estes MK, Preidis GA.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
screening_reason: The study identifies gut microbiota-derived branched-chain fatty acids (isovalerate) as crucial regulators of intestinal junction complexes and barrier function.
summary_ja: 低タンパク質・低脂質食による栄養不良モデルマウスを用いて、腸内細菌叢とその代謝物が腸管バリア機能に与える影響を解析した。栄養不良の雄性SPFマウスにおいてのみ、大腸粘液層の薄層化、腸管透過性の亢進、および細菌移行が観察された一方、無菌マウスや雌性マウスではバリア障害が生じなかった。代謝物解析により、栄養不良下では分岐鎖脂肪酸（BCFA）であるイソ吉草酸が枯渇していることが判明した。ヒトオルガノイドや雄性マウスへのイソ吉草酸またはその前駆体ロイシンの投与は、タイトジャンクションタンパク質claudin-8の局在を改善し、腸管バリア機能を回復させた。
summary_en: Malnutrition induced colonic mucus thinning, increased permeability, and bacterial translocation in male specific-pathogen-free mice, but not in germ-free or female mice. Targeted metabolomics revealed that microbial-derived branched-chain fatty acids (BCFAs), particularly isovalerate, were depleted during malnutrition. Treatment with isovalerate or its dietary precursor leucine restored claudin-8 expression and rescued intestinal barrier integrity.
key_finding_ja: 栄養不良によって減少する腸内細菌由来の分岐鎖脂肪酸（イソ吉草酸）が、雄性マウスにおける性特異的な腸管バリア機能障害を改善することを突き止めた。
why_it_matters_ja: 腸内細菌代謝物を標的とした精密栄養療法（ロイシン補給など）が、栄養不良に伴う腸管バリア障害や全身性感染症リスクの低減に貢献する可能性がある。

title: Integrated multi-omics analysis identifies microbial and metabolic signatures and drivers of CNS autoimmunity.
abstract: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is an autoimmune disease of the central nervous system (CNS), driven by genetic and environmental determinants. The gut microbiome of people with MS (pwMS) is distinct and influences disease through immunomodulatory metabolite production. Circulating metabolites are altered in pwMS, but identifying microbial-metabolic drivers remains challenging. We previously showed that colonization by the gut commensal Limosilactobacillus reuteri exacerbates disease in the experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE) model of MS in a tryptophan-dependent manner. Here, we integrated microbiomic and metabolomic data sets from a longitudinal EAE study utilizing high- and low-tryptophan diets in mice colonized with or without L. reuteri . Gut microbiome dynamics, under short- and long-term alterations in tryptophan bioavailability, were affected by diet, microbiome context, or disease. During short-term dietary intervention, L. reuteri colonization exerted a greater impact on microbiome composition than tryptophan bioavailability. With longer dietary exposure and EAE progression, high dietary tryptophan and L. reuteri colonization synergized to elicit profound microbiota changes, including alterations in Lachnospiraceae, Blautia, and Akkermansia . Integration of metabolomic and microbiomic data sets using joint Robust Aitchison PCA revealed clusters of associated metabolites and microbiota enriched for functional pathways, including bile acid and tryptophan metabolism. Metabolites outperformed microbiota in predicting EAE severity, identifying p-cresols and indoles as top disease-associated metabolites. Treatment with p-cresol or 3-indoleglyoxylic acid exacerbated EAE, enhanced proinflammatory T-cell responses, and increased cerebellar pathology. These data demonstrate that dietary responses are shaped by gut microbiome composition and that integrated microbiomic-metabolomic analyses can identify the drivers of disease worsening in MS.IMPORTANCEMultiple sclerosis (MS) is a multifactorial disease influenced not only by genetics but also by environmental factors, potentially including diet and the composition of the gut microbiome. We show that interactions between diet and commensal gut microbiota profoundly impact the levels of immunomodulatory systemic metabolites, including several that are associated with disease in people with MS (pwMS). Importantly, we demonstrate that individual gut microbiota-produced metabolites are sufficient to worsen disease in a mouse model of MS. Integration of gut microbiome and blood metabolite data sets, combined with subsequent predictive modeling, may bolster biomarker identification and the capacity to predict disease severity in pwMS, as compared to the performance of individual data sets alone. These findings highlight metabolites as key mediators linking diet and the gut microbiota to neuroinflammation. Importantly, this work suggests that targeting microbial metabolites or modifying diet-microbiome interactions may represent new strategies to reduce disease activity in MS and related autoimmune disorders.
authors: Montgomery TL, Nelson EA, Downs LA, Heney ER, Lee MFJ, Martino C, McDonald D, Rahman G, Knight R, Krementsov DN.
screening_reason: The study explores how gut microbiome composition and microbial metabolites drive central nervous system autoimmunity and neuroinflammation in an EAE model.
summary_ja: 多発性硬化症（MS）モデルマウスにおいて、トリプトファン代謝および腸内細菌Limosilactobacillus reuteriの定着が中枢神経系自己免疫に与える影響を多層的オミクス解析により評価した。食事中のトリプトファン量とL. reuteriの定着は相乗的に作用し、腸内細菌叢の構成および代謝物プロファイルを大きく変化させた。統合データ解析から、p-クレゾールやインドール類が病態の重症度を強力に予測する代謝物として同定された。実際にp-クレゾールや3-インドールグリオキシル酸の投与は、前炎症性T細胞応答の増強や小脳病変の悪化を介してEAE病態を直接悪化させた。
summary_en: Integrating microbiomic and metabolomic datasets from an EAE mouse model revealed that Limosilactobacillus reuteri colonization and high dietary tryptophan synergistically altered gut microbiota composition and systemic metabolites. Metabolites such as p-cresols and indoles strongly predicted EAE severity. Treatment with p-cresol or 3-indoleglyoxylic acid exacerbated EAE symptoms, enhanced proinflammatory T-cell responses, and increased cerebellar pathology.
key_finding_ja: 腸内細菌と食事成分の相互作用によって産生されるp-クレゾールやインドール化合物の増大が、中枢神経系自己免疫疾患マウスの炎症性T細胞応答を増強し病態を悪化させることが示された。
why_it_matters_ja: 食事と腸内細菌叢の相互作用を介して産生される代謝物を標的とすることが、多発性硬化症などの神経炎症性疾患に対する新たな治療介入法につながる可能性がある。

title: Immunopharmacological mechanisms underlying SARS-CoV-2 spike-induced persistent pain in mice.
abstract: SARS-CoV-2 infection is frequently associated with persistent pain, yet the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. Given that viral structural proteins can act as pathogen-associated molecular patterns, we investigated whether the Spike protein is sufficient to induce long-lasting nociceptive alterations and the immune pathways involved. Intraplantar administration of recombinant Spike protein in mice elicited robust and persistent mechanical and thermal hypersensitivity, accompanied by transient local inflammation, sustained systemic cytokine alterations, and prolonged spinal neuroinflammation. Spike-induced paw inflammation and persistent mechanical hypersensitivity were dependent on Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4), as both pharmacological inhibition and genetic deficiency of TLR4 abolished these responses. Mechanistically, depletion of mononuclear phagocytes or blockade of T-cell co-stimulation prevented the development of persistent mechanical hypersensitivity, supporting a role for coordinated innate and adaptive immune mechanisms in the establishment of long-lasting nociceptive sensitization. In parallel, Spike induced increases in lymphocyte-associated cytokines, including IFN-γ, IL-4, and IL-17, with modest and transient changes in peripheral compartments but pronounced and sustained elevations in the spinal cord. Among these, IFN-γ emerged as a critical contributor to these responses, as its genetic deletion abolished both inflammation and persistent hypersensitivity. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that the SARS-CoV-2 Spike protein is sufficient to trigger persistent pain-like states through a TLR4-driven neuroimmune cascade involving phagocytes, T cells, and IFN-γ signaling. This study provides mechanistic insight into neuroimmune pathways that may contribute to persistent pain following SARS-CoV-2 infection and establishes a tractable mechanistic experimental model for investigating Spike-induced neuroimmune mechanisms of chronic pain.
authors: de Lima Almeida B, Pereira S, Primicheru LI, Vitorino LC, Goldoni FC, Fernandes OKF, Rasga GL, da Cruz Nunes M, Manjavachi MN, D'Oliveira GSM, Freixo PF, de Matos Guedes HL, Figueiredo CP, Quintão NLM, Bevan S, Passos GF, da Costa R.
screening_reason: Mechanistic study demonstrating that SARS-CoV-2 Spike protein induces chronic pain via a TLR4-dependent neuroimmune cascade and spinal neuroinflammation.
summary_ja: SARS-CoV-2のスパイクタンパク質がマウスにおいて持続的な痛覚過敏を引き起こす免疫薬理学的メカニズムを解明した研究である。足底へのスパイクタンパク質投与は、局所炎症だけでなく持続的な脊髄の神経炎症と機械的・熱的痛覚過敏を誘発した。この病態はTLR4依存的であり、単核食細胞の除去やT細胞共刺激の阻害、あるいはIFN-γの遺伝子欠損により過敏状態が消失した。したがって、スパイクタンパク質は食細胞やT細胞、IFN-γシグナルが関与するTLR4駆動型神経免疫カスケードを介して持続痛を引き起こす。
summary_en: Intraplantar administration of SARS-CoV-2 Spike protein in mice induced persistent pain-like hypersensitivity and sustained spinal neuroinflammation. This response was mediated by TLR4 and required mononuclear phagocytes, T-cell co-stimulation, and IFN-γ signaling. The study demonstrates that Spike protein alone is sufficient to trigger long-lasting pain via a specific neuroimmune axis.
key_finding_ja: SARS-CoV-2のスパイクタンパク質は、TLR4、食細胞、T細胞、およびIFN-γが関与する神経免疫カスケードを介して持続的な痛覚過敏を誘導する。
why_it_matters_ja: SARS-CoV-2感染後に生じる持続性疼痛のメカニズム解明や、神経免疫経路を標的とした治療法開発に寄与する可能性がある。

title: Dysbiosis of the oral-gut microbiome axis in a mouse model of depression.
abstract: This study aimed to characterize the alterations in both oral and gut microbiota in a mouse model of depression and to explore their potential role in the pathogenesis of major depressive disorder (MDD) through the oral-gut-brain axis. A depression model was established in male C57BL/6J mice using chronic social defeat stress (CSDS) paradigm. Depressive phenotypes were confirmed through social interaction, sucrose preference, open field, tail suspension, and forced swim tests. The microbial composition of oral and gut samples was analyzed using 16S rRNA sequencing, with Linear Discriminant Analysis Effect Size (LEfSe) employed to identify differentially abundant taxa and Spearman correlation analysis to examine microbiota-behavior relationships. CSDS successfully induced robust depression-like behaviors, including social avoidance, anhedonia, and behavioral despair. Beta-diversity analysis revealed significant separation in oral microbiota between CSDS and control groups. LEfSe analysis identified distinct microbial signatures: control mice were enriched in oral Streptococcus and gut commensals including Lachnospiraceae, Bacteroides and Oscillospiraceae, whereas CSDS mice showed expansion of oral Muribacter and Rodentibacter and gut Alloprevotella, Helicobacter and Colidextribacter. Correlation analyses demonstrated significant associations between specific microbial patterns and depression-like behaviors, with control-enriched taxa negatively correlating with behavioral deficits. Furthermore, significant cross-habitat microbial correlations were observed between oral and gut differential taxa. Our findings demonstrate that CSDS induces divergent microbial alterations in both oral and gut ecosystems, which are systematically associated with depression-like behaviors. These results provide compelling evidence for the involvement of the oral-gut-brain axis in depression pathophysiology and suggest that modulating these microbial ecosystems may represent a potential therapeutic strategy for MDD.
authors: Lei P, Tong S, Xi W, Liu Y, Yu J, Yu L, Zhao B, Jia M, Li Y, Ma X, Wang Y, Guo Y.
screening_reason: Directly investigates oral and gut microbiome alterations and their association with depression-like behaviors in a mouse model.
summary_ja: 慢性的社会的挫折ストレス（CSDS）によるうつ病マウスモデルを用いて、口腔および腸内細菌叢の変化を解析した。16S rRNAメタゲノム解析により、対照群とうつ病モデル群で口腔および腸内の細菌組成が大きく異なることが示された。対照群では口腔 Streptococcus や腸内 Lachnospiraceae などが豊富であったのに対し、CSDS群では口腔 Muribacter や腸内 Alloprevotella などが増加していた。特定細菌の存在比はうつ様行動と相関し、口腔と腸の細菌間にも相互関連が認められた。
summary_en: Using a chronic social defeat stress mouse model of depression, this study evaluated alterations in oral and gut microbiota via 16S rRNA sequencing. CSDS mice exhibited distinct microbial signatures compared to controls, including the expansion of specific oral and gut taxa. These microbial patterns significantly correlated with depression-like behaviors and revealed cross-habitat correlations between oral and gut communities.
key_finding_ja: 慢性的社会的挫折ストレスを与えたマウスでは、口腔および腸内の細菌叢に特徴的な構成変化が生じ、それらがうつ様行動と有意に相関していた。
why_it_matters_ja: 口腔・腸・脳軸を介したマイクロバイオームの変動が抑うつ病態に関与する可能性を示しており、細菌叢の調節が新たな治療戦略につながるかもしれない。

title: Bile acids as mediators of microbiota signaling in entero-hepatic disorders.
abstract: This review examines the structure and the functional role of the signaling network formed by bile acids as their receptors in mediating chemical communication between the intestinal microbiota and host in entero-hepatic disorders, such as inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) and Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease (MASLD). In the last decade, advances in analytical technologies and bioinformatic approaches, including metabolomics and reverse metabolomics, have greatly expanded our understanding of bile acid metabolism. These studies have shown that the intestinal microbiota transforms primary bile acids synthesized in the liver from cholesterol into a highly diverse family of bioactive mediators. Hundred of "classical" secondary bile acids and Microbial Derived Bile Acids (MDBA) have been identified and characterized for their role in regulating the activity of widely expressed receptors, including the Farnesoid-x-receptor (FXR), the G protein-coupled bile acid receptor (GPBAR1) and the retinoid-related orphan receptor (RORγ). Simultaneous characterization of microbial species expressing bile acid-related genes is emerging as a valuable tool for disease phenotyping. One example is bile salt hydrolase (BSH), an enzyme that catalyzes bile acid deconjugation. In parallel, profiling bile acid composition in biological compartments such as feces and blood may help identify associations between microbiota dysbiosis and diseases including IBD and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH). The review also examines therapeutic approaches that could be developed to exploit this novel conceptual framework.
authors: Fiorucci S, Marchianò S, Giorgio CD, Urbani G, Monti MC, Zampella A, Distrutti E, Biagioli M.
screening_reason: The paper examines host-microbe interactions, intestinal microbial metabolism of bile acids, and host receptor signaling in entero-hepatic disorders.
summary_ja: 本レビューは、炎症性腸疾患（IBD）や代謝異常関連脂肪肝疾患（MASLD）などの腸肝疾患における、腸内細菌叢と宿主間のシグナル伝達物質としての胆汁酸の役割を解説している。メタボロミクス技術の進展により、腸内細菌が一次胆汁酸を多様な生物活性を持つ二次胆汁酸や微生物由来胆汁酸へ変換することが明示された。これらの胆汁酸はFXRやGPBAR1、RORγなどの受容体を介して機能し、胆汁酸塩水解酵素（BSH）などの酵素遺伝子を保有する菌種の同定が病態分類に利用されている。著者らは糞便や血液中の胆汁酸プロファイル解析と概念的枠組みに基づく治療法開発の可能性を論じている。
summary_en: This review discusses bile acids as key molecular signaling links between the gut microbiota and the host in entero-hepatic disorders, such as inflammatory bowel disease and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease. Advanced metabolomic approaches have revealed that gut bacteria convert liver-derived primary bile acids into a diverse pool of bioactive secondary bile acids and microbial-derived bile acids that target receptors like FXR and GPBAR1. The authors highlight the potential of profiling microbial bile acid-metabolizing pathways for disease phenotyping and novel therapeutic target discovery.
key_finding_ja: 腸内細菌が生成する多種多様な二次胆汁酸および微生物由来胆汁酸が、宿主の胆汁酸受容体を介して腸肝疾患の病態調節を担うシグナル因子であることが概括された。
why_it_matters_ja: 胆汁酸代謝を中心とした腸内細菌叢と宿主の相互作用の解明は、炎症性腸疾患や代謝性肝疾患の精密な病態診断や新たな治療法開発につながる可能性がある。

title: Astrocyte-Microglia Crosstalk in Post-Hemorrhagic Neurovascular Microenvironment: Mechanistic Nodes, Cross-Stroke Comparisons, and Therapeutic Reprogramming.
abstract: Background Intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) produces a rapidly evolving and spatially heterogeneous neurovascular microenvironment in which secondary injury is shaped not only by hematoma volume and location, but also by the interaction of blood-derived toxins, blood-brain barrier disruption, edema, oxidative stress, protease activity, and glial responses. Increasing evidence suggests that these processes are better understood as dynamic network events rather than isolated inflammatory pathways. Main body This review applies a network-centered framework to astrocyte-microglia coupling, viewing it as a critical control layer that may either support injury containment and hematoma resolution or drive persistent neurotoxicity and failed repair. Comparisons with ischemic stroke are used to distinguish shared inflammatory modules from hemorrhage-specific drivers, including heme, hemoglobin, iron overload, thrombin, fibrinogen, and clot-associated protease signaling. Integrating findings from single-cell and spatially resolved studies, the review summarizes the temporal and spatial organization of post-hemorrhagic microenvironment remodeling and discusses astrocyte-dependent regulation of barrier function, edema dynamics, immunometabolism, redox buffering, and synaptic homeostasis. It also examines how astrocyte-derived cues influence microglial state transitions through danger sensing, inflammasome signaling, cyclic GMP-AMP synthase-stimulator of interferon (IFN) genes signaling, phagocytic containment, iron-handling programs, complement-mediated synaptic vulnerability, and interaction with infiltrating myeloid cells. Recurring astrocyte-microglia network motifs are further evaluated as therapeutic control points, with emphasis on how lesion stage and spatial compartmentalization shape intervention windows for purinergic, chemokine, cytokine, IFN, complement-coagulation, and lipid/iron signaling pathways. Translational priorities, limitations, and therapeutic opportunities are discussed across hematoma-toxicity reduction, barrier and edema repair, network reprogramming, and regenerative microenvironment shaping. Conclusion Meaningful improvement in ICH outcome will likely depend on biomarker-guided and stage-specific reprogramming of astrocyte-microglia network dynamics to restore microenvironmental balance, rather than on nonspecific suppression of neuroinflammation.
authors: Ye F, Chen R, Xu S, Liu H, Xu J.
screening_reason: The review focuses centrally on astrocyte-microglia crosstalk, neuroinflammatory cascades, and microglial state transitions following intracerebral hemorrhage.
summary_ja: 本レビュー論文は、脳内出血後の微小環境におけるアストロサイトとミクログリアの相互作用とその役割を網羅的に解説している。著者らは、出血後に生じる複雑な病態現象を単一の炎症経路ではなく、動的なネットワーク応答として捉える重要性を提示した。血腫由来毒素やヘム、鉄過剰などの出血特異的因子と虚血性脳卒中の共通因子を比較し、ミクログリアのフェノタイプ変化やアストロサイトのバリア調節機構をまとめている。また、病期や局所特異性に応じた制御ポイントを同定し、神経炎症の制御に向けた治療戦略を論じた。
summary_en: This review outlines the dynamic network interactions between astrocytes and microglia within the neurovascular microenvironment following intracerebral hemorrhage. By comparing hemorrhagic pathways with ischemic stroke modules, the authors highlight how hemorrhage-specific factors like heme and iron overload shape glial responses and microenvironmental remodeling. The article emphasizes that stage- and region-specific therapeutic reprogramming of astrocyte-microglia networks represents a more effective strategy than non-specific neuroinflammation suppression.
key_finding_ja: 脳内出血後のアストロサイトとミクログリアの網羅的ネットワーク解析に基づき、病期に応じた相互作用の再プログラミングが新たな治療アプローチとして提案された。
why_it_matters_ja: 脳内出血の二次的損傷を抑制するためには、単なる微小炎症の抑制ではなく病期や空間的特性に応じた細やかな神経免疫ネットワークの制御が重要であることが示唆される。

title: Antibiotic Mixture Exposure in Meconium Affects Child Neurodevelopment via Altering Early-Life Gut Microbiome and Metabolome.
abstract: Previous evidence has established associations of antibiotic exposure in early life with neurodevelopmental disorders. However, previous studies have often relied on self-reported or record-based exposure measures that may not accurately reflect internal fetal exposure, and few have integrated prenatal exposure biomarkers with infant microbiome, metabolome, and longitudinal neurodevelopmental data. This study included 300 mother-infant pairs from the Shanghai Maternal-Child Pairs Cohort. Meconium samples were used to quantify concentrations of 18 antibiotics using high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC). Neurodevelopmental outcomes were assessed using Ages and Stages Questionnaires (ASQ) at 2, 6, 12, and 24 months of age. Multi-omics profiling of 6-month fecal samples was conducted, employing 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing and HPLC-based metabolomics. Linear and logistic regression models, negative binomial regression, interpretable machine learning algorithms, metabolome-wide association/pathway analyses and high-dimensional mediation modeling were used. Our study population demonstrated predominant exposure to three antibiotics: chlortetracycline, penicillin, and chloramphenicol. Each interquartile range (IQR) increase in meconium-measured antibiotic burden was associated with a lower total ASQ score at 6 months (β = -4.49, 95% CI: -7.14 to -1.86) and lower scores across all five developmental domains (βs ranging from -0.53 to -1.11; all P < 0.05). Each IQR increment of antibiotic burden was also associated with greater odds of belonging to the lower-score group of total ASQ trajectory (OR = 1.20, 95% CI: 1.04, 1.42) and the lower-score group of personal-social trajectory (OR = 1.13, 95% CI: 1.01, 1.28). Exploratory high-dimensional mediation analyses identified Lactobacillus and 2-(14,15-epoxyeicosatrienoyl) glycerol (2-14,15-EG) as candidate intermediates in the association between meconium-measured antibiotic burden and neurodevelopment. Our study suggested that higher meconium-based biomarkers of intrauterine antibiotic burden were significantly associated with lower neurodevelopmental outcomes in early childhood, with the strongest inverse associations observed at 6 months. Lactobacillus and 2-14,15-EG were identified as potential mediator biomarkers. These hypothesis-generating findings require independent replication, longitudinal temporal validation, and experimental studies before causal mechanisms or microbiota-targeted interventions can be inferred.
authors: Zhou Y, Wang F, Zhao Y, Wang H, Ma W, Shi H, Zhang Y.
screening_reason: The study investigates how intrauterine antibiotic exposure affects child neurodevelopment through changes in early-life gut microbiome composition and microbial metabolomics.
summary_ja: 母子コホート300組を対象に、胎便中の18種類の抗菌薬濃度測定と生後6か月時の腸内細菌叢・代謝物メタボローム解析を行い、24か月までの神経発達との関連を調べた。胎便中の抗菌薬暴露量が多いほど、生後6か月時点のASQスコア低下および低い発達トラジェクトリーに属するリスクの上昇が観察された。高次元媒介解析により、Lactobacillus属と代謝物2-14,15-EGが抗菌薬暴露と神経発達低下を結ぶ潜在的な仲介因子として特定された。胎児期の抗菌薬暴露が乳幼児の神経発達に悪影響を与える可能性が示唆された。
summary_en: In a prospective cohort of 300 mother-infant pairs, meconium antibiotic levels were quantified alongside infant gut microbiome and metabolome profiles at 6 months to assess child neurodevelopment through 24 months. Higher internal fetal antibiotic exposure correlated with lower neurodevelopmental scores and persistently poorer developmental trajectories. Mediation analyses indicated that infant Lactobacillus levels and the metabolite 2-14,15-EG candidate-mediated these neurodevelopmental impacts.
key_finding_ja: 胎児期の抗菌薬暴露負荷は乳幼児の神経発達低下と関連し、乳児期の腸内細菌Lactobacillusと代謝物2-14,15-EGがその媒介候補として同定された。
why_it_matters_ja: 周産期抗菌薬使用のリスク評価や腸内細菌叢を介した予防介入法の開発に役立つ可能性があるが、因果関係の解明にはさらなる実証研究が必要である。

title: SIK2-P300 axis Orchestrates the metabolic reprogramming and Immunological functions in microglia of Alzheimer's disease mice via a dual modulation of lactylation and Acetylation: An epigenetic Perspective.
abstract: Metabolic dysfunction in microglia is increasingly recognized as a core driver of Alzheimer's disease (AD) pathogenesis, and yet the underlying mechanisms remain elusive. Here, we identified salt-inducible kinase 2 (SIK2) as a critical metabolic checkpoint that was downregulated in microglia across the AD mouse models (5 × FAD, APP/PS1, and SAMP8). We found that a loss of SIK2 in microglia induced a pro‑inflammatory phenotype, thus impairing amyloid β-protein (Aβ) phagocytosis and rewiring glucose and lipid metabolism toward enhanced glycolysis and lipid accumulation. Mechanistically, SIK2 directly interacted with the histone acetyltransferase P300; SIK2 deficiency increased the activity of P300, elevating H3K9 acetylation and H4K8/12 lactylation at promoters of metabolic genes. The microglia‑specific SIK2 overexpression in the 5 × FAD mice mitigated cognitive deficits, Aβ pathology, neuroinflammation, and aberrant histone modifications. A pharmacological inhibition of P300 regained these protective effects. Our findings highlight the SIK2-P300 epigenetic axis as a key regulator of the metabolic homeostasis in microglia and a potential therapeutic target for AD treatments.
authors: Dai X, Ye Z, Zhang X, Huang Y, Wang C, Liu Y, Gao B, Zhang J, Chen X.
screening_reason: Investigates microglial neuroinflammation along with histone post-translational modifications (acetylation and lactylation).
summary_ja: アルツハイマー病マウスモデルのミクログリアにおいて、塩誘導性キナーゼ2（SIK2）の発現低下が確認された。SIK2の欠損はプロ炎症性フェノタイプを誘導し、アミロイドβの食作用を障害するとともに、解糖系および脂質蓄積を亢進させる代謝改変を引き起こした。メカニズムとして、SIK2欠損によりヒストンアセチルトランスフェラーゼP300の活性が上昇し、代謝関連遺伝子プロモーターにおけるH3K9アセチル化とH4K8/12ラクチル化が増加した。5×FADマウスでのSIK2過剰発現やP300阻害は、認知機能の低下や異常なヒストン修飾を改善させた。
summary_en: Researchers identified SIK2 downregulation in microglia across Alzheimer's disease mouse models, which drove pro-inflammatory phenotypes and metabolic rewiring toward enhanced glycolysis. SIK2 deficiency increased P300 activity, leading to elevated histone H3K9 acetylation and H4K8/12 lactylation at metabolic gene promoters. Overexpressing SIK2 or inhibiting P300 restored microglial metabolic homeostasis and mitigated cognitive deficits in 5xFAD mice.
key_finding_ja: SIK2-P300軸がヒストンのアセチル化およびラクチル化を双方向に制御し、ADマウスにおけるミクログリアの代謝恒常性と免疫機能を決定することが明かとなった。
why_it_matters_ja: ミクログリアにおけるエピジェネティックな翻訳後修飾メカニズムの解明は、アルツハイマー病の新たな代謝標的治療の開発につながる可能性がある。

title: P2X7 Signaling in Neuroinflammation: Glial Crosstalk, Redox Integration, and Therapeutic Targeting.
abstract: Extracellular ATP is a central danger signal linking cellular stress to neuroinflammation, yet the mechanisms governing the transition from physiological purinergic signaling to pathological neuroimmune activation remain incompletely understood. In this review, we integrate current evidence into a conceptual framework describing how ATP-dependent purinergic signaling may contribute to the shift from adaptive neuron-glia communication to maladaptive glial crosstalk and inflammatory amplification. Under physiological conditions, controlled ATP turnover primarily engages lower-threshold purinergic pathways, including P2X4-mediated signaling that supports microglial surveillance, synaptic remodeling, and tissue homeostasis. In contrast, sustained extracellular ATP accumulation during injury, oxidative stress, or impaired ATP clearance preferentially recruits the low-affinity P2X7 receptor, triggering ionic dysregulation, Ca²⁺ influx, and redox-sensitive signaling pathways that promote NF-κB activation and NLRP3 inflammasome assembly. We further examine how receptor crosstalk, particularly with TLR4 and emerging redox regulatory mechanisms involving protein disulfide isomerase (PDI), may influence P2X7 signaling across different neuroinflammatory contexts. Finally, we discuss current evidence for therapeutic targeting of P2X7, highlighting translational challenges related to blood-brain barrier penetration, receptor occupancy, disease stage, and patient selection. By integrating recent advances in purinergic, redox, and neuroimmune signaling, this review provides a heuristic framework for understanding context-dependent P2X7 activation while distinguishing established mechanisms from emerging concepts that require further experimental validation.
authors: Ayyubova G, Sultanova T, Gurbanova S, Ayyubova N.
screening_reason: Focuses on purinergic P2X7 receptor signaling in driving microglial neuroinflammation and neuroimmune crosstalk.
summary_ja: 本レビューでは、細胞外ATPが適応的な神経・グリア間コミュニケーションから病理学的な神経炎症へと移行させる役割を整理している。通常時は低閾値のP2X4経路がミクログリアのサーベイランスや組織恒常性を維持するのに対し、持続的なATP蓄積下では低親和性P2X7受容体が優先的に応答する。P2X7の活性化はイオン平衡異常やカルシウム流入、NF-κB活性化やNLRP3インフラマソーム形成を誘発する。さらにTLR4やプロテインジスルフィドイソメラーゼを介した酸化還元制御とのクロストーク、および治療標的としての課題を論じている。
summary_en: This review synthesizes mechanisms by which extracellular ATP transitions from physiological purinergic signaling to pathological neuroinflammation. High ATP levels engage low-affinity P2X7 receptors, driving ionic dysregulation, Ca2+ influx, and activation of NF-kB and the NLRP3 inflammasome. The authors highlight crosstalk with TLR4 and redox regulators like PDI, alongside translational challenges in targeting P2X7.
key_finding_ja: P2X7受容体は高濃度の細胞外ATPに依存して活性化し、酸化還元反応や受容体クロストークを伴って神経炎症を増幅させることが説明された。
why_it_matters_ja: P2X7受容体の病理的メカニズムと創薬上の課題の統合的理解は、神経炎症性疾患に対する新たな治療アプローチの考案に寄与する可能性がある。

title: Intermittent fasting alleviates neuropathic pain and cognitive deficits via an Alistipes finegoldii-Hippuric Acid-STING neuroimmune axis.
abstract: Chronic pain is frequently accompanied by cognitive and affective impairments, yet effective non-pharmacological interventions remain limited. Here, we show that intermittent fasting (IF) alleviates mechanical allodynia, thermal hyperalgesia, and cognitive deficits across multiple chronic pain models, and reduces anxiety-like behavior in the chronic constriction injury (CCI) model. IF strengthened intestinal barrier integrity, reduced neuroinflammation, and reshaped the gut microbiota, with Alistipes finegoldii (A. finegoldii) emerging as the most consistently enriched species. Supplementation with live A. finegoldii recapitulated the analgesic and pro-cognitive effects of IF. Integrated metabolomics identified hippuric acid as the key IF-responsive metabolite, and systemic hippuric acid administration restored pain, cognitive, and anxiety-like behaviors in CCI mice. Mechanistically, both IF and hippuric acid downregulated the STING (Stimulator of Interferon Genes) neuroimmune pathway, and pharmacological STING activation abolished the therapeutic effects of hippuric acid, establishing STING inhibition as a mechanistic requirement. Genomic annotation predicted that A. finegoldii contains homologs of enzymes consistent with the potential to generate benzoate, which could enable host co-metabolism to hippuric acid. Together, these findings identify an IF-A. finegoldii-hippuric acid-STING axis that links microbial metabolism to neuroimmune modulation and behavioral improvement, highlighting microbiota-derived metabolites as promising targets for treating chronic pain and its cognitive comorbidities.
authors: Ding X, Qiu D, Li XY, Qiao YH, Hashimoto K, Wang XM, Yang JJ.
screening_reason: The study demonstrates a gut microbiota-derived metabolite axis (Alistipes finegoldii and hippuric acid) modulating neuroimmune STING signaling and neuropathic pain.
summary_ja: 慢性疼痛モデルマウスにおいて、間欠的断食（IF）が神経障害性疼痛、認知機能障害、不安様行動に及ぼす影響とその分子機構を解析した。IFの介入は腸管バリア機能を強化し、神経炎症を軽減するとともに、腸内細菌Alistipes finegoldiiを特異的に増加させた。オミクス解析により見出された代謝物馬尿酸の投与やA. finegoldiiの生菌補充は、IFと同様に鎮痛および認知機能改善効果を発揮した。機構としてIFおよび馬尿酸はSTING神経免疫経路を抑制しており、薬理学的STING活性化によってこれらの治療効果が消失することが確認された。
summary_en: Intermittent fasting (IF) alleviated neuropathic pain and cognitive impairments in chronic pain mouse models by reinforcing gut barrier integrity, dampening neuroinflammation, and enriching Alistipes finegoldii. Systemic administration of hippuric acid, a key IF-responsive metabolite associated with A. finegoldii metabolism, mimicked the therapeutic effects of IF. Mechanistically, IF and hippuric acid attenuated behavioral deficits by downregulating the STING neuroimmune signaling pathway.
key_finding_ja: 間欠的断食はAlistipes finegoldiiの増殖と馬尿酸の産生を介してSTING神経免疫経路を抑制し、慢性疼痛や認知機能障害を軽減させる。
why_it_matters_ja: 腸内細菌由来の代謝物を介した神経免疫調節機構の解明は、慢性疼痛およびその精神・認知行動異常に対する非薬物療法の開発につながる可能性がある。

title: In vitro metabolic signaling in two intestinal bacterial isolates: glutamate-driven transcriptional and functional reprogramming in Clostridium butyricum and Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron .
abstract: Monosodium glutamate (MSG; L-glutamate monosodium salt) is among the most widely used flavor enhancers, yet its molecular effects on gut microbial physiology remain poorly understood. Here, we examined the strain-specific transcriptomic and metabolic responses of Clostridium butyricum and Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron grown in pure anaerobic culture with 0.1% (wt/vol) MSG. Although MSG exposure was not associated with major changes in total bacterial biomass dynamics, both species showed a temporal functional reprogramming. In C. butyricum , MSG rapidly intensified metabolic activity to capitalize on exogenous glutamate by activating central carbon metabolism, redox-balancing pathways, and the GABA shunt, thereby collectively enhancing butyrate synthesis, a metabolite associated with gut barrier integrity, energy regulation, and anti-inflammatory signaling. On the other hand, B. thetaiotaomicron adopted a conservative, homeostatic response, suppressing glycan utilization and central carbon and energy metabolism, and maintaining stable SCFA production through controlled regulation that buffered against abrupt dietary perturbations. Overall, MSG functioned as a potent metabolic signal, triggering distinct adaptive strategies in two dominant gut bacteria. Importance The impact of monosodium glutamate (MSG) as a highly consumed food additive on the gut microbiome is often overlooked, and community-level analyses reveal little change, masking distinct phenotypic responses of individual strains. By combining gene expression and metabolite profiling using two key human gut bacteria, we show that MSG is sensed as a metabolic signal. A butyrate-producing gut bacterium increases energy metabolism and butyrate production, and a fiber-degrading gut bacterium transiently moderates metabolism to maintain stable fermentation products. These differences suggest that MSG's physiological effects may depend on which bacterial groups dominate an individual's microbiome.
authors: Nematzadeh Somehsaraei N, Lemuel Hadi J, Khan Mirzaei M, Deng L, Gigl M, Dawid C, Schmitt-Kopplin P, Geydirici I, Schloter M, Gschwendtner S.
screening_reason: The study directly investigates metabolic signaling, transcriptomic changes, and short-chain fatty acid production in human gut bacterial isolates.
summary_ja: 調味料として広く使用されるグルタミン酸ナトリウム（MSG）が腸内細菌の生理機能に与える分子レベルの影響を調べるため、Clostridium butyricumとBacteroides thetaiotaomicronの純粋培養下での応答を解析した。MSGの添加は全体的な細菌増殖動態には大きな影響を与えなかったが、両菌株において特異的な代謝再編成を引き起こした。C. butyricumは中央炭素代謝やGABAシャントを活性化させて酪酸産生を増強させた一方、B. thetaiotaomicronは代謝活動を一時的に抑制し短鎖脂肪酸の安定した産生を維持した。以上の結果から、MSGは特定の腸内細菌に対して異なる適応戦略を誘発する代謝シグナルとして機能することが明らかになった。
summary_en: This study investigated the strain-specific transcriptomic and metabolic responses of Clostridium butyricum and Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron to monosodium glutamate (MSG) exposure in vitro. While MSG did not alter overall bacterial biomass dynamics, it triggered distinct functional reprogramming in each species. C. butyricum enhanced energy metabolism and butyrate synthesis via the GABA shunt and central carbon metabolism, whereas B. thetaiotaomicron adopted a conservative metabolic response to maintain stable short-chain fatty acid production.
key_finding_ja: グルタミン酸ナトリウムは腸内細菌の代謝シグナルとして機能し、C. butyricumにおける酪酸産生増強やB. thetaiotaomicronにおける代謝調節など菌株特異的な適応応答を誘発する。
why_it_matters_ja: 食事性食品添加物が特定の腸内細菌の代謝活性を選択的に変化させる可能性が示され、個人ごとの腸内細菌叢に応じた生理的影響の理解につながることが期待される。

title: Gut microbiome: a key driver and therapeutic target of intestinal fibrosis in Crohn's disease.
abstract: Intestinal fibrosis is a debilitating complication of Crohn's disease that often leads to stricture formation, requiring surgical intervention. Despite its clinical significance, effective anti-fibrotic therapies remain an unmet need. Emerging evidence highlights the gut microbiome as a central orchestrator of fibrogenesis, beyond its role in inflammation. This review provides a comprehensive overview of how microbial dysbiosis, which is marked by the expansion of pathobionts such as adherent-invasive Escherichia coli and Clostridium innocuum, drives intestinal fibrosis through multifaceted pathways. We delineate the direct activation of fibroblasts via pattern recognition receptors and indirect mechanisms involving macrophage polarization, T helper 17 cell responses, and the emerging role of the "creeping fat" axis. Furthermore, we discuss how microbial translocation into the mesenteric adipose tissue triggers a profibrotic environment. By synthesizing these mechanistic insights, we suggest that targeting the microbiome-fibrosis axis, through precision modulation of the microbiome or metabolite-based interventions, represents a promising frontier for preventing and reversing fibrostenotic Crohn's disease.
authors: Kim JH, Choi YJ, Yoo JH.
screening_reason: Comprehensive mechanistic review detailing how gut microbial dysbiosis drives intestinal fibrosis in Crohn's disease.
summary_ja: クローン病における合併症である腸管線維化と腸内細菌叢との関連をまとめたレビュー論文である。付着侵襲性大腸菌や Clostridium innocuum などの病原体様細菌の増加が、線維芽細胞の直接活性化や免疫細胞・脂肪組織を介して線維化を進行させることが解説されている。腸間膜脂肪組織への細菌転移が線維化促進環境を形成するメカニズムも議論されている。マイクロバイオームや代謝物を標的とした精密な介入が、線維化の予防・逆転における新たな治療法となる可能性を提示している。
summary_en: This review summarizes the role of the gut microbiome as a driver and therapeutic target of intestinal fibrosis in Crohn's disease. Pathobionts like AIEC and Clostridium innocuum promote fibrogenesis through direct fibroblast activation and indirect neuroimmune/inflammatory responses. Precision targeting of the microbiome-fibrosis axis represents a promising therapeutic approach for fibrostenotic Crohn's disease.
key_finding_ja: クローン病における腸管線維化は、特定の病原体様細菌が線維芽細胞や脂肪組織・免疫系を介して引き起こす複合的な機序によって推進される。
why_it_matters_ja: 細菌叢やその代謝物を標的とする新しい精密治療法が、難治性であるクローン病の狭窄・線維化の克服に寄与する可能性がある。

title: Global gut microbiome atlas identifies epidemiologic-stage-specific signatures in inflammatory bowel disease.
abstract: The global rise of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) reflects environmental shifts, yet how these changes are embedded in the gut microbial ecology remains unclear. We construct a microbiome atlas comprising 245,627 profiles. By classifying countries into three epidemiologic stages, we establish a framework. As the IBD burden increases, the gut microbial alpha diversity declines, and community structures form distinct clusters. This transition is characterized by a gradient of core genera. Integrating six shotgun metagenomic cohorts, we identify the depletion of anabolic pathways in IBD patients. Strain-level analysis reveals that epidemiologic staging shapes genetic architecture within species, identifying an IBD-enriched subclade of Eisenbergiella associated with elevated fecal cholic acid. We develop a microbial inflammatory risk score (MIRS), based on 19 genera, that discriminates IBD from controls (area under the curve [AUC] = 0.92). MIRS correlates with IBD prevalence. Our study provides an atlas linking epidemiology to microbiome ecology and strain evolution, offering a foundation for population-level surveillance and interventions in IBD.
authors: Zhai J, Li Y, Liu J, Su X, Cui R, Zheng D, Sun Y, Yu J, Dai C.
screening_reason: Constructs a global gut microbiome atlas to identify stage-specific gut microbial signatures and functional pathways in inflammatory bowel disease.
summary_ja: 24万サンプル以上のマイクロバイオームデータから、炎症性腸疾患（IBD）の疫学段階に応じた世界的な腸内細菌叢アトラスを構築した。IBDの疾患負担が大きい地域ほど、腸内細菌叢のα多様性が低下し、特異な群集構造を示すことが明らかになった。メタゲノム解析によりIBD患者での同化経路の欠損や、コール酸上昇に関連する Eisenbergiella の特定のサブクレードが特定された。さらに、19の属に基づく細菌性炎症リスクスコア（MIRS）を開発し、高い精度でIBDを識別できることを示した。
summary_en: A global gut microbiome atlas of 245,627 profiles was constructed to identify signatures across epidemiologic stages of inflammatory bowel disease. Higher IBD disease burden correlated with decreased alpha diversity and specific genus-level shift patterns. The study identified IBD-associated metabolic shifts, strain-level evolution in Eisenbergiella, and established a 19-genus risk score that effectively discriminates IBD.
key_finding_ja: IBDの地域的疫学段階に対応した腸内細菌叢アトラスを構築し、高い精度でIBDを識別する19属ベースの微生物リスクスコアを開発した。
why_it_matters_ja: 集団レベルでのIBDの監視や生態学的知見に基づいた介入手法の基盤となる可能性がある。

title: Does high fructose consumption trigger microglia activation and neuroinflammation? A systematic review.
abstract: This systematic review evaluated the effects of fructose intake on neuroinflammatory markers in rodent models. The search terms Fructose AND neuroinflammation OR Neurodegeneration OR chemokines OR interleukins OR microglia OR behaviour OR memory OR cognition were used in Google Scholar, Scopus and Web of Science. Thirteen animal studies investigating fructose-induced neuroinflammation that matched the eligibility criteria were included in the study. Across the studies, 16 inflammatory markers were identified as significantly altered following exposure to fructose. The findings consistently demonstrated elevated expression of pro-inflammatory cytokines, TNF-α, IL-6, and IL-1β, following fructose administration. Fructose consumption also dysregulated MCP-1, fractalkine, and CX3CR1 levels, thereby promoting inflammatory signalling and microglial activation. Furthermore, fructose exposure significantly increased IBA-1 and CD11b, indicating sustained neuroimmune activation. Alterations in important inflammatory pathways involving TLR4, NLRP3, NF-κB, MyD88, iNOS, and cyclooxygenases (COX-1 and COX-2) were also observed. In contrast, expression of the anti-inflammatory regulator peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma (PPARγ) was reduced after fructose treatment. Overall, the findings suggest that chronic fructose consumption induces neuroinflammation through multiple inflammatory and immune-related mechanisms in the brain. These effects appear to be dose- and duration-dependent and may contribute significantly to neurodegeneration and cognitive impairment.
authors: Olasehinde TA, Hernandez-Ledesma B, Cortes-Gomez P, Olaokun O, Olaniran AO.
journal: Food and chemical toxicology : an international journal published for the British Industrial Biological Research Association
screening_reason: The systematic review evaluates microglial activation, pro-inflammatory signaling pathways, and neuroinflammation induced by high fructose consumption.
summary_ja: 本系統的レビューは、果糖（フルクトース）の過剰摂取が齧歯類モデルの脳内神経炎症に与える影響を調査した13件の動物実験論文を評価した。解析の結果、果糖投与によりTNF-α、IL-6、IL-1βなどの前炎性サイトカインの上昇が共通して確認された。さらに、IBA-1やCD11bの発現増加によるミクログリアの持続的活性化や、TLR4、NLRP3、NF-κB経路の異常活性化が観察された。一方で抗炎症に関与するPPARγの発現低下も確認され、果糖の持続的摂取が用量および期間依存的に脳内神経炎症を引き起こすことが示された。
summary_en: This systematic review evaluated 13 animal studies examining the impact of chronic fructose intake on neuroinflammatory responses in rodent models. The findings consistently demonstrated that fructose consumption elevated pro-inflammatory cytokines, activated microglial markers such as IBA-1 and CD11b, and dysregulated signaling pathways including TLR4, NLRP3, and NF-κB. These results suggest that high fructose intake induces dose- and duration-dependent neuroinflammation, which may contribute to neurodegeneration and cognitive decline.
key_finding_ja: 齧歯類モデルに関する系統的レビューにより、高果糖摂取が前炎性サイトカインの増加およびミクログリアの活性化を介して脳内神経炎症を誘発することが確認された。
why_it_matters_ja: 食習慣による果糖の過剰摂取が脳内の神経免疫系に悪影響を及ぼし、認知機能低下や神経変性疾患のリスクを上昇させる可能性が示唆される。

title: Antisense transcription reveals disease-associated adaptations in the human gut microbiome.
abstract: The gut microbiome is a dynamic ecosystem in which microorganisms constantly adjust their transcriptional programmes. Here we developed metastrand, a framework that integrates strand-aware metatranscriptomics and metagenomics to quantify mRNAs and antisense RNAs (asRNAs) in complex microbial communities at gene-level resolution. In inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), microbial asRNA programmes converged across patients during active disease, correlated with faecal metabolites and calprotectin levels and remained stable during persistent inflammation, highlighting their potential as biomarkers of inflammatory activity in the gut. These programmes involved antisense-to-sense transcriptional shifts at insertion sequence elements with functionally diverse passenger genes and preceded their detection at new genomic locations, linking asRNA dynamics to structural genome rearrangements and redistribution of adaptive functions under selective pressure. Similar dynamics were observed in a mouse model of colitis, oxidative stress in vitro and in patients with pathogen-confirmed gastroenteritis, establishing asRNAs as an important dimension of microbial adaptation in health and disease.
authors: Pust MM, Mohamed AMT, Stražar M, Arias-Rojas A, Cunningham-Oakes E, Brown EM, Bumber A, Pishchany G, Li C, Ananthakrishnan AN, Darby AC, Vlamakis H, Plichta DR, Xavier RJ.
screening_reason: The paper focuses on metatranscriptomic profiling of antisense RNA dynamics and transcriptional adaptation within the human gut microbiome.
summary_ja: 本研究では、ストランド認識型メタトランスクリプトミクスとメタゲノミクスを統合し、腸内細菌叢のアンチセンスRNA（asRNA）を高解像度で定量する解析ツール「metastrand」を開発した。炎症性腸疾患（IBD）患者の活動期において細菌のasRNA発現パターンが収束し、便中カルプロテクチンなどの炎症指標と相関することが示された。asRNAの動態は挿入配列エレメントにおけるアンチセンスからセンスへの転写シフトを引き起こし、ゲノム構造の再編に先立って適応機能を提示していた。同様の現象はマウスの大腸炎モデルや病原体感染性胃腸炎患者でも確認され、asRNAが病態適応の重要な要素であることが明らかになった。
summary_en: Researchers established metastrand, an analytical platform integrating strand-aware metatranscriptomics and metagenomics to quantify bacterial mRNA and antisense RNA dynamics. In inflammatory bowel disease, gut microbial antisense RNA profiles converged during active disease and correlated with fecal inflammatory markers. These antisense RNA shifts preceded genomic rearrangements, demonstrating that antisense transcription serves as a key mechanism for microbial adaptation during inflammation.
key_finding_ja: 腸内細菌のアンチセンスRNA転写動態は、炎症性腸疾患などの病態におけるゲノム再編と環境適応を駆動する。
why_it_matters_ja: 腸内細菌の病態適応メカニズムの理解を深め、炎症性腸疾患の新たな診断バイオマーカーや治療標的の開発につながる可能性がある。

title: Biomimetic exosomal delivery of ginsenoside Rd reduces post-stroke depression via microglial reprogramming in a pathway involving EGFR/JAK2/STAT3.
abstract: Post-stroke depression (PSD) represents a complex neuropsychiatric challenge characterized by persistent neuroinflammation and synaptic dysfunction, yet effective therapeutic interventions are constrained by the blood-brain barrier (BBB) and the lack of specific targets. Using a multidimensional screening strategy for Chaihu-Jia-Longgu-Muli Decoction (CLM), we identified ginsenoside Rd (Rd) as a key blood-absorbed bioactive constituent associated with Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor (EGFR) signaling. To overcome the bioavailability bottleneck, a biomimetic nanodelivery system is engineered by encapsulating Rd into microglia-derived exosomes (Exos@Rd). Based on the reported lesion-homing properties of microglia-derived exosomes, we developed a biomimetic Exos@Rd delivery system. Exosomal loading markedly enhanced the brain accumulation of Rd compared with free Rd. Mechanistically, it is demonstrated that aberrant EGFR activation functions as an upstream regulator of the JAK2/STAT3 cascade in microglia. Exos@Rd effectively suppressed this pathway and promoted anti-inflammatory microglial reprogramming, characterized by a shift from an M1-associated pro-inflammatory state toward an M2-associated anti-inflammatory profile. This microglia-centered anti-inflammatory regulation was accompanied by reduced oxidative stress and restoration of brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF), postsynaptic density protein 95 (PSD95) and Synapsin I (SYN1) expression. In a PSD mouse model, Exos@Rd significantly restores cerebral perfusion and alleviates depressive-like behaviors. Collectively, this study elucidates a novel EGFR-driven neuroinflammatory mechanism and presents a bio-inspired strategy for precision CNS drug delivery, offering a promising therapeutic paradigm for PSD.
authors: Chen J, Yin X, Yan D, Shi Q, Tan E, Yan Z, Zhang P, Li W, Xiao M, Wang Q, Fan Q, Li P, Liu J.
screening_reason: The study focuses on microglial anti-inflammatory reprogramming and neuroinflammation modulation in post-stroke depression.
summary_ja: 脳卒中後うつ病（PSD）は持続的な神経炎症と神経伝達の機能障害を特徴とするが、血流脳関門の存在が標的治療の障害となっている。本研究では、ミクログリア由来エクソソームにジンセノシドRdを内包させたナノ製剤（Exos@Rd）を構築し、脳内送達効率を大幅に向上させた。メカニズム解析により、ミクログリアにおけるEGFR/JAK2/STAT3経路の過剰活性化が神経炎症を誘導すること、ならびにExos@Rdが同経路を抑制してM2抗炎症型表現型への再プログラミングを促進することが示された。PSDマウスモデルにおいて、Exos@Rd投与は脳血流を改善し、シナプス関連因子の発現を回復させてうつ様行動を軽減させた。
summary_en: To address the therapeutic challenges of post-stroke depression, researchers engineered a biomimetic exosomal delivery system encapsulating ginsenoside Rd (Exos@Rd). Exos@Rd targeted microglial aberrant EGFR activation and suppressed the downstream JAK2/STAT3 signaling cascade, promoting anti-inflammatory microglial reprogramming. In a mouse model of post-stroke depression, Exos@Rd treatment restored cerebral perfusion, reduced oxidative stress, upregulated synaptic markers, and significantly attenuated depressive-like behaviors.
key_finding_ja: ミクログリア由来エクソソームで送達したジンセノシドRdは、EGFR/JAK2/STAT3経路を抑制してミクログリアを抗炎症型に再プログラミングし、脳卒中後うつ病モデルマウスの症状を改善した。
why_it_matters_ja: 脳卒中後うつ病の病態におけるEGFRシグナルの関与が明らかになり、エクソソームを利用した脳指向性ナノドラッグデリバリーの有用性が示された。

title: Microbiome-Inflammation-Mitochondria Coupling in Neurodegeneration and Depression: An Integrative Opinion.
abstract: There is increasing evidence that gut microbiome dysbiosis, systemic inflammation, and mitochondrial dysfunction interact in ways that influence psychiatric and neurodegenerative disease vulnerability. Recent findings indicate that microbial signaling, inflammatory activation, and mitochondrial stress responses form dynamic bidirectional networks that may influence neurotransmission, neuroplasticity, metabolism, and behavior. This integrative opinion article distinguishes major depressive disorder (MDD), Parkinson's disease (PD), and Alzheimer's disease (AD) as mechanistically distinct disorders while proposing that they may share overlapping upstream modulatory pathways involving inflammation, microbial dysregulation, and mitochondrial dysfunction. Importantly, the microbiome-inflammation-mitochondria axis is presented as a disease-modifying and vulnerability-associated framework rather than a singular unifying etiology. Current limitations including reverse causation, microbiome heterogeneity, and differences in treatment responsiveness are also discussed.
authors: Stefano GB, Esch T.
screening_reason: The article details the bidirectional interaction between gut microbiome dysbiosis, systemic/neuroinflammation, and mitochondrial function in neurodegeneration.
summary_ja: 本論文は、大うつ病性障害（MDD）、パーキンソン病（PD）、アルツハイマー病（AD）における腸内細菌叢の乱れ、全身性炎症、ミトコンドリア機能障害の相互作用に関する意見論文である。著者らは、これら3つの疾患が異なる病態メカニズムを持ちつつも、上流の共通した修飾経路を共有している可能性を提案している。また、この軸は単一の病因ではなく、病態修飾および脆弱性に関連するフレームワークとして提示されている。さらに、逆の因果関係や腸内細菌叢の多様性、治療反応性の違いといった現状の課題についても論じている。
summary_en: This opinion article proposes that gut microbiome dysbiosis, systemic inflammation, and mitochondrial dysfunction form dynamic networks influencing vulnerability to psychiatric and neurodegenerative disorders. The authors emphasize that major depressive disorder, Parkinson's disease, and Alzheimer's disease share overlapping upstream pathways while remaining mechanistically distinct. The microbiome-inflammation-mitochondria axis is framed as a disease-modifying network rather than a single etiology, while addressing key limitations such as heterogeneity and reverse causation.
key_finding_ja: 腸内細菌叢、全身性炎症、ミトコンドリア機能障害の軸が、精神疾患および神経変性疾患における共通の上流修飾経路として作用している可能性が提示された。
why_it_matters_ja: 本フレームワークは多様な神経精神疾患の理解に向けた新たな視点を提供するが、因果関係の立証や個人差の考慮には更なる検証が必要である。

title: Multi-level aggregation analysis of microbiome composition and host gene expression reveals associations with systemic and local immunity.
abstract: The human gut microbiome plays a critical role in immune regulation, yet the molecular links between microbiome composition and host gene expression remain incompletely understood. We analyzed associations between host gene expression and microbiome composition in a cohort of 315 healthy individuals, integrating microarray-based gene expression data from three intestinal sites (ileum, transverse colon, and rectum) and six immune cell types with microbiome sequencing data. Using a hierarchical feature aggregation strategy combining principal component analysis, clustering, and covariate correction, we discovered significant associations primarily related to immunity. While microbial profiles were similar across the three intestinal sites, the transverse colon yielded the most "microbiome-host gene expression" associations. Among the immune cell types, CD8+ cells showed the highest number of associations. The first principal component of microbiome composition, reflecting a gradient from commensals (e.g., Ruminococcaceae and Christensenellaceae ) to proinflammatory taxa ([ Ruminococcus ] gnavus and Lachnoclostridium ), correlated with the expression of TNF-α-linked genes ( HMOX1 , CPI17 , HSD3B2 , and SLC5A1 ). Among individual genera, Catenibacterium abundance was associated with gene expression in both intestinal and immune cells, including negative associations with MRPS21 (related to mitochondrial function) in the transverse colon and with CD8+ gene programs related to T cell differentiation. These findings align with emerging evidence implicating mitochondrial dysfunction in intestinal inflammation. Our results identify multi-level associations between the gut microbiome and host gene expression, suggesting potential mechanisms by which microbiota shape local and systemic immunity and vice versa. The implicated genes and taxa represent candidates for experimental validation to improve understanding of host-microbiome homeostasis and its disruption in disease.IMPORTANCEThe gut microbiome and immune system are engaged in a complex interplay throughout human life. While most associative studies focus on case-control comparisons-typically examining patients with conditions such as inflammatory bowel disease or metabolic diseases-less is known about the molecular links between the microbiome and immune system in healthy individuals. In this study of a large cohort of healthy individuals, we addressed this gap by applying multiscale modeling to tackle the high dimensionality of host-microbiome data. We identified multi-level associations between microbiome composition and host gene expression in both intestinal tissues and immune cells. These findings offer a valuable reference for understanding baseline host-microbiome communication and highlight molecular candidates-such as TNF-α-related genes and mitochondrial pathways-for future experimental validation.
authors: Shagam LI, Elizarova A, Momozawa Y, Dmitrieva J, Mariman R, Rahmouni S, Louis E, Georges M, Tyakht AV, Klimenko N.
screening_reason: The study investigates interactions between human gut microbiome composition, microbial taxa, and host gene expression in mucosal and immune tissues.
summary_ja: 健常者315名のコホートを対象に、腸管3部位の組織および6種類の免疫細胞における遺伝子発現と腸内細菌叢データの関連を解析した。細菌叢の主要な構成傾斜は、TNF-αに関連する遺伝子群の発現と相関を示した。部位別では横行結腸、細胞種別ではCD8陽性T細胞において最も多くの関連が特定された。また、Catenibacterium属の存在量はミトコンドリア機能やT細胞分化に関連する遺伝子プログラムと負の関連を示した。
summary_en: Using a cohort of 315 healthy individuals, this study analyzed associations between gut microbiome composition and host gene expression across three intestinal sites and six immune cell types. The primary gradient of microbiome composition correlated with TNF-a-linked gene expression, with the highest number of associations observed in the transverse colon and CD8+ immune cells. Genus-level analyses revealed that Catenibacterium abundance was negatively associated with mitochondrial and T-cell differentiation gene programs.
key_finding_ja: 健常者において腸内細菌叢の構成が、局所的な腸管組織および全身の免疫細胞における遺伝子発現と多層的に関連していることが実証された。
why_it_matters_ja: 健常状態における腸内細菌叢と免疫系の恒常性維持機構を理解するための基盤データとなるが、同定された候補遺伝子の機能検証が求められる。

title: Modulating the gut-joint axis: Bifidobacterium longum subsp. infantis B8762 is associated with selective gut microbial and metabolic alterations in knee osteoarthritis.
abstract: Knee osteoarthritis (KOA) is a debilitating degenerative joint disorder characterized by chronic low-grade inflammation and metabolic dysregulation. The gut microbiota has emerged as an important regulator of systemic inflammatory responses. Building upon our previous clinical findings that Bifidobacterium longum subsp. infantis B8762 (B8762) improved clinical symptoms and inflammatory markers in patients with KOA, the present study investigated the associated alterations in the gut microbiome and fecal metabolome. Fecal samples were collected from probiotic (n = 20) and placebo (n = 20) groups at baseline (0 M) and after a 1-month intervention (1 M). Integrated metagenomic and untargeted metabolomic analyses were performed to characterize changes in gut microbial composition, functional potential, and metabolic profiles. Metagenomic reads mapped to the B8762 reference genome showed a greater increase in B8762-associated mapping rates in the probiotic group than in the placebo group, supporting an association between B8762 supplementation and longitudinal changes in the gut microbiome. Longitudinal analysis further demonstrated greater increases in microbial alpha diversity in the probiotic group. Species-level analyses suggested selective alterations in gut microbial composition, with nominally higher relative abundances of Bifidobacterium pseudocatenulatum and Anaerostipes caccae and lower relative abundances of Holdemania filiformis and Lachnospira SGB5077 (nominal P < 0.05). HUMAnN3-based functional profiling identified enrichment of microbial pathways related to carbon utilization and amino acid biosynthesis, including the bifidobacterial shunt and branched-chain amino acid biosynthesis pathways. Untargeted metabolomics identified nominal between-group differences in metabolites primarily related to lipid metabolism, including lower relative abundances of aldosterone and 7α-hydroxy-4-cholesten-3-one in the probiotic group (nominal P < 0.05). Correlation analysis further revealed associations between differential taxa and selected metabolites, suggesting potential links between gut microbial alterations and steroid-related metabolic pathways. Overall, B8762 supplementation was associated with longitudinal changes in B8762-associated genomic signals, gut microbial diversity and composition, microbial functional potential, and fecal metabolic profiles.
