These findings provide exploratory multi-omics evidence supporting an association between B8762 supplementation and gut microbial-metabolic remodeling in KOA and generate hypotheses for future mechanistic studies of the gut-joint axis.
authors: Yang L, Zhao J, Han T, Qi H, Zhao F, Sun Z.
screening_reason: The study evaluates alterations in gut microbiome diversity, composition, and fecal microbial metabolic pathways following probiotic intervention.
summary_ja: 変形性膝関節症（KOA）患者40名を対象に、Bifidobacterium longum subsp. infantis B8762（B8762）摂取群20名とプラセボ群20名による1ヶ月間の介入研究を実施した。糞便のメタゲノムおよび非標的メタボローム解析により、プロバイオティクス群でB8762関連ゲノムシグナルやα多様性の有意な増加が確認された。特定菌種の相対存在量の変化とともに、炭素利用やアミノ酸合成に関連する微生物機能経路の濃縮が認められた。また、アルドステロンなどの脂質代謝に関連する糞便代謝物の群間差が観察された。
summary_en: In a 1-month trial involving knee osteoarthritis patients divided into probiotic and placebo groups (n = 20 each), B8762 supplementation was evaluated using metagenomic and untargeted metabolomic analyses. Probiotic intake was associated with increases in B8762-mapped reads, microbial alpha diversity, and selective alterations in specific gut taxa and functional pathways. Untargeted metabolomics identified nominal between-group differences in lipid-related metabolites, suggesting potential links between gut microbial changes and host metabolic pathways.
key_finding_ja: 変形性膝関節症患者におけるB8762の摂取は、腸内細菌叢の多様性・組成・機能的経路および糞便代謝物プロファイルの変化と関連していた。
why_it_matters_ja: 腸-関節軸を介した病態改善メカニズムの可能性が示されたが、臨床的有効性や因果関係の確定には更なる大規模検証が必要である。

title: A gut microbiome-lipid axis in early pregnancy is associated with metabolic dysregulation and diabetes risk.
abstract: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) reflects metabolic dysregulation that becomes clinically apparent during pregnancy and shares key pathophysiological features with broader forms of diabetes. Gut microbiome-host metabolic interactions may contribute to this process, yet their role in early pregnancy remains incompletely understood. In this prospective nested case-control study within the Tongji-Huaxi-Shuangliu Birth Cohort, 784 pregnant women, including 222 who developed GDM, underwent first-trimester gut metagenomic and plasma lipidomic profiling. Cross-omics analyses were performed to identify microbiome-lipid associations and potential mediation patterns. Women who later developed GDM showed reduced gut microbial diversity and altered microbial profiles in early pregnancy. We identified 26 microbial species associated with GDM risk, with seven species, including Ruminococcus bicirculans ( R. bicirculans ), showing concordant associations in external type 2 diabetes populations. Microbial pathways related to fatty acid and lipid biosynthesis were enriched in women at higher risk. Plasma lipidomics revealed widespread alterations, particularly among glycosphingolipid-related metabolites. Integrated analyses suggested that lipidomic variation statistically accounted for part of the microbiome-GDM association. A class-level dihexosylceramide feature, DHC 24:1, consistent with lactosylceramide-related metabolites, emerged as a potential mediator and was prioritized for exploratory follow-up. Experimental analyses provided functional support for a microbiome-lipid-host interaction axis. R. bicirculans promoted lactosylceramide 24:1 production in vitro , bacterial colonization and metabolite administration improved insulin tolerance in vivo , and lactosylceramide 24:1 modulated insulin-stimulated AKT signaling dynamics in hepatocytes. These findings identify a gut microbiome-lipid axis associated with metabolic dysregulation in pregnancy and suggest a potential mechanism linking microbial metabolism to host insulin signaling.
authors: Sun Z, He C, Ma X, Wu P, Wang T, Yuan J, Pu Y, Zhou X, Mei Z, Song H, Wang Y, Yue H, Fu Y, Zheng J, Pan A, Chen D, Hong S, Pan XF, Zheng Y.
screening_reason: Demonstrates a gut microbiome-lipid axis where bacterial species and microbial metabolites modulate host metabolic signaling.
summary_ja: 妊娠初期の腸内細菌叢と脂質代謝異常および妊娠糖尿病（GDM）リスクとの関連を検討したコホート研究である。GDMを発症した妊婦では妊娠初期の腸内細菌多様性が低下し、26種の細菌種や脂質合成に関連する代謝経路の変動が観察された。実験解析では、Ruminococcus bicirculansがジヘキソシルセラミド代謝物（DHC 24:1）の産生に関与し、インスリン抵抗性やシグナル伝達を調節することが実証された。これらの知見は、妊娠中のインスリン抵抗性を媒介する腸内細菌-脂質-宿主相互作用の存在を示唆している。
summary_en: A prospective nested case-control study was conducted to analyze first-trimester gut metagenomics and plasma lipidomics in pregnant women. Decreased microbial diversity and alterations in 26 microbial species, including Ruminococcus bicirculans, were associated with subsequent gestational diabetes mellitus risk. Mechanistic experiments supported a gut microbiome-lipid axis wherein R. bicirculans and its lipid metabolite influence host insulin signaling.
key_finding_ja: 妊娠初期の腸内細菌叢の変動と特定のセラミド関連脂質代謝物が妊娠糖尿病リスクおよびインスリンシグナル調節に関連することが示された。
why_it_matters_ja: 妊娠初期における代謝異常の早期予測や、腸内細菌叢を標的とした代謝疾患予防戦略の開発につながる可能性がある。

title: Impaired Glur2 palmitoylation in cerebellar Purkinje cells of a Friedreich ataxia mouse model.
abstract: Friedreich's ataxia (FRDA) is a neurodegenerative disorder caused by frataxin deficiency, characterized by progressive cerebellar dysfunction and neuronal loss. Although synaptic abnormalities are an early feature of FRDA, the molecular mechanisms linking frataxin deficiency to synaptic dysfunction remain incompletely defined. In this study, we investigated post-translational regulation of the AMPA receptor subunit GluR2 in the cerebellum of the frataxin knockdown (FRDAkd) mouse model. GluR2 protein levels are reduced early following frataxin knockdown, despite unchanged mRNA expression and preserved Purkinje cell number. Phosphorylation of GluR2 at regulatory sites (Ser880 and Tyr876) are unchanged relative to total protein, indicating that altered phosphorylation does not account for reduced GluR2 levels. In contrast, acyl-biotin exchange assays and proximity ligation analysis reveal a significant reduction in GluR2 palmitoylation, localized primarily to Purkinje cell somata. This deficit is selective, as palmitoylation of other synaptic proteins is variably affected. Mechanistically, reduced GluR2 palmitoylation associates with decreased expression and palmitoylation of the palmitoyl acyltransferase DHHC3, while levels of depalmitoylating enzymes remain unchanged. In vitro, DHHC3 enhances GluR2 palmitoylation, supporting a direct enzymatic relationship. Partial restoration of frataxin expression rescues GluR2 and DHHC3 protein levels and partially restores GluR2 palmitoylation. These findings identify impaired GluR2 palmitoylation as an early, selective synaptic alteration in FRDA and implicate dysregulated lipid-dependent post-translational modification as a mechanism linking frataxin deficiency to cerebellar synaptic vulnerability.
authors: Mercado-Ayón E, Coulman J, Lee JY, Lancaster E, Goga E, Asad M, Witze E, Lynch DR.
screening_reason: Mechanistic investigation of impaired protein post-translational modification (GluR2 palmitoylation by DHHC3) in a model of Friedreich's ataxia.
summary_ja: フリードライヒ運動失調症（FRDA）モデルマウスの小脳におけるAMPA受容体サブユニットGluR2の翻訳後修飾制御を検討した。フラタキシン低下に伴い、GluR2のmRNA発現量は維持されるもののタンパク質レベルおよびパルミトイル化修飾が特異的に減少していた。この現象はパルミトイル基転移酵素DHHC3の発現低下およびパルミトイル化低下と関連していた。フラタキシンの部分的な発現回復によりGluR2およびDHHC3のタンパク質レベルとパルミトイル化が一部回復した。
summary_en: This study examined the post-translational regulation of the AMPA receptor subunit GluR2 in a frataxin-knockdown mouse model of Friedreich's ataxia. Frataxin deficiency led to a selective reduction in GluR2 palmitoylation in cerebellar Purkinje cells, which was associated with decreased expression and palmitoylation of the palmitoyltransferase DHHC3. Restoring frataxin expression partially rescued both DHHC3 and GluR2 levels and palmitoylation status.
key_finding_ja: フリードライヒ運動失調症モデルにおいて、小脳プルキンエ細胞におけるGluR2のパルミトイル化障害が初期のシナプス病態に関与している。
why_it_matters_ja: 脂質依存的な翻訳後修飾の異常がフラタキシン欠損による小脳シナプス機能障害を媒介している可能性を示しており、新たな治療標的の解明に寄与する。

title: Gastrointestinal dysfunction associated with autoimmune glial fibrillary acidic protein astrocytopathy.
abstract: Background and objectives Gastrointestinal (GI) dysfunction has been reported in autoimmune glial fibrillary acidic protein astrocytopathy (GFAP-A). However, GI dysfunction in GFAP-A has not been sufficiently investigated. This study aimed to analyze the clinical features of GFAP-A patients with GI dysfunction and explore potential pathogenic mechanisms. Methods From January 1, 2016, to April 30, 2024, patients diagnosed with GFAP-A based on CSF GFAP-IgG positivity at the Third Affiliated Hospital of Sun Yat-sen University were enrolled. Clinical parameters and GI dysfunction assessed by the I-FEED scoring system were collected. Pathological examination was performed in a subset of patients. And the preliminary role of GFAP-IgG in the enteric plexus was investigated. Results Among 92 enrolled individuals (male:female = 68:24; median age 39.5 years), gastrointestinal dysfunction occurred in 72 cases (78.3%). Manifestations included constipation in 38 cases (41.3%), paralytic ileus in 30 cases (32.6%), fecal incontinence in 3 cases (3.26%), and diarrhea in 1 case (1.09%). Severe GI dysfunction (I-FEED score ≥ 6) was associated with higher disease severity (admission mRS 5.0 vs. 3.0, p Conclusions Our findings collectively suggest that severe GI dysfunction could be a marker of disease severity and poor prognosis in GFAP-A, and indicate that its potential mechanism may involve the specific binding of anti-GFAP-IgG to the enteric plexus and subsequent enteric glia loss.
authors: Xiao L, Qin B, Guo Y, Zhang P, Lu Y, Wang Y, Lai W, Chen J, Ke B, Huang L, Sun J, Qiu W, Pan Y, Long Y, Shu Y.
screening_reason: Investigates gastrointestinal dysfunction in GFAP astrocytopathy, focusing on anti-GFAP-IgG interaction with the enteric plexus and enteric glia loss.
summary_ja: 自己免疫性GFAPアストロサイトパチー（GFAP-A）患者における消化管機能障害の臨床的特徴と病態メカニズムを調査した。92例の患者を評価した結果、78.3%に便秘や麻痺性イレウスなどの消化管機能障害が認められた。重度の消化管機能障害（I-FEEDスコア6以上）は高い疾患重症度や転帰不良と有意に関連していた。病理学的検討などから、抗GFAP-IgGの腸管神経叢への結合および腸管グリア細胞の消失が病態に関与している可能性が示唆された。
summary_en: This study investigated gastrointestinal dysfunction in 92 patients with autoimmune GFAP astrocytopathy. Gastrointestinal symptoms occurred in 78.3% of patients, with severe dysfunction correlating with higher clinical severity and poorer prognosis. Pathological and mechanistic analyses suggested that anti-GFAP-IgG targeting of the enteric plexus and subsequent enteric glial loss contribute to this dysfunction.
key_finding_ja: 自己免疫性GFAPアストロサイトパチー患者の約78%に消化管障害が認められ、その重症度は全身の病勢および腸管グリア脱落と相関していた。
why_it_matters_ja: GFAPアストロサイトパチーにおける消化管症状が重症度予測の指標となる可能性があり、腸管神経系への自己抗体反応の評価が臨床上重要となり得る。

title: The Positive Feedback Interaction Between Mast Cell-Derived Tryptase and NETs Formation in the Pathogenesis of Sepsis-Associated Encephalopathy.
abstract: Background Sepsis-associated encephalopathy (SAE) is a serious neurological complication resulting from sepsis, marked by considerable neuroinflammation and deficits in cognitive function. While neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) have been implicated in various neuroinflammatory conditions, the specific mechanisms underlying NETs formation in SAE, particularly the role of brain-resident mast cells (MCs) and their interplay with neutrophils, remain poorly understood. Methods The cecal ligation and puncture (CLP) procedure was employed to create the SAE model in male C57BL/6 mice. Comprehensive methodological approaches included: 1) Pharmacological interventions using MC stabilizer (cromolyn), MC activator (C48/80), tryptase inhibitor (APC366), and Protease-activated receptor 2(PAR2) antagonist (AZ3451); 2) Establishment of MC-neutrophil co-culture systems with PMA/LPS stimulation; 3) Advanced imaging techniques including multiplex immunofluorescence and NETs visualization through Cit-H3/MPO/DAPI triple staining; 4) Molecular pathway analysis through Western blot, co-immunoprecipitation, and lactate quantification; 5) Functional assessments of MC activation through β-hexosaminidase release and tryptase activity assays. Results MC activation significantly promoted neutrophil infiltration and NET formation in SAE mice. Investigations into the mechanisms have demonstrated that tryptase, derived from MC, activates the PAR2-MAPK signaling pathway in neutrophils, which results in an increased expression of LDHA and boosts lactate production. Subsequently, lactate-mediated lactylation stabilizes PAD4 protein by inhibiting its degradation, thereby facilitating NETosis. Furthermore, NETs promote a positive feedback mechanism by boosting MC activation and elevating the release and activity of tryptase, thereby creating a self-reinforcing cycle of inflammation. Conclusion This study elucidates a novel bidirectional MC-NETs axis in SAE pathogenesis, wherein tryptase-PAR2-MAPK signaling and lactylation-mediated PAD4 stabilization drive progressive neuroinflammation. These findings not only advance our understanding of SAE mechanisms but also identify multiple potential therapeutic targets within this pathway for clinical intervention.
authors: Peng Y, Mo L, Zeng G, Xu X, Zhang X, Cheng Y, Jiang Y, Yue J.
screening_reason: Elucidates a neuroimmune axis involving mast cell-neutrophil interaction and NETosis driving neuroinflammation in sepsis-associated encephalopathy.
summary_ja: 敗血症関連脳症（SAE）のマウスモデルを用いて、肥満細胞と好中球の相互作用機構を検証した。肥満細胞由来のトリプターゼが好中球のPAR2-MAPK経路を活性化し、LDHA発現と乳酸産生を促進することが明らかになった。乳酸を介したラクチル化修飾によってPAD4タンパク質が安定化しNETosisが促進され、形成されたNETsがさらに肥満細胞を活性化する正のフィードバック環を形成していた。
summary_en: Using a cecal ligation and puncture mouse model of sepsis-associated encephalopathy (SAE), this study identified a positive feedback loop between mast cells and neutrophils. Mast cell-derived tryptase activated PAR2-MAPK signaling in neutrophils, increasing lactate production and lactylation-mediated stabilization of PAD4 to drive NETosis. In turn, NETs further stimulated mast cell activation and tryptase release, establishing a self-reinforcing inflammatory cycle.
key_finding_ja: 敗血症関連脳症において肥満細胞由来トリプターゼと好中球NETs形成が相互に活性化し合う正のフィードバック回路が神経炎症を増悪させることが解明された。
why_it_matters_ja: SAEの病態メカニズムにおける神経免疫相互作用の重要性を示しているが、人体における臨床的有効性や安全性については今後の検証を要する。

title: The NETs-cGAS-STING Axis in Ischemic Stroke: Linking Neutrophil-Microglia Crosstalk, Immunothrombosis, and Neuroinflammation.
abstract: The immune and inflammatory responses following ischemic stroke involve aberrant DNA exposure, immunothrombosis, and innate immune activation. Post-stroke, damage-associated DNA signals from multiple sources may activate DNA-sensing pathways; however, how DNA from distinct sources links peripheral immune activation with inflammatory amplification within the brain remains incompletely understood. Among these, neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs), as DNA-rich extracellular structures, may represent a potential link connecting vascular inflammation, immunothrombosis, and intracerebral DNA sensing. The cyclic GMP-AMP synthase-stimulator of interferon genes (cGAS-STING) pathway, a key DNA-sensing axis, mediates distinct inflammatory and stress responses across various stroke-associated cell types. This review summarizes the mechanisms of DNA recognition, NET-mediated immunothrombosis, and neuroinflammatory damage, as well as the functional characteristics of cGAS-STING signaling in different cell types. Based on current evidence, we propose a potential NETs-cGAS-STING inflammatory amplification framework: NET-derived DNA may contribute to DNA-sensing activation within the ischemic brain and promote microglial inflammatory responses, while the resulting inflammatory factors and chemotactic signals may further promote neutrophil recruitment and secondary NET formation, thereby potentially creating a feed-forward loop linking peripheral immune activation with neuroinflammation. We further discuss the spatiotemporal heterogeneity of this axis, therapeutic targets, and challenges for clinical translation. Overall, the NETs-cGAS-STING framework provides an integrated conceptual perspective for understanding the intercellular interactions underlying DNA recognition and the sustained amplification of inflammation following stroke, and offers insights into future precision immune interventions tailored to disease stage, lesion characteristics, and cell-specific responses.
authors: Yang L, Liu J, Luo S, Zeng Q, Li D, Deng Y.
screening_reason: Explores neutrophil-microglia crosstalk and cGAS-STING-mediated neuroinflammation in ischemic stroke.
summary_ja: 本総説は、虚血性脳卒中後の好中球細胞外トラップ（NETs）とcGAS-STING経路による炎症増幅機構について整理している。脳虚血領域においてNETs由来のDNAがcGAS-STING経路を介してミクログリアの炎症反応を刺激する可能性が論じられている。活性化したミクログリアから放出される因子がさらなる好中球の動員と二次的なNETs形成を促進するポジティブフィードバック回路が提案されている。さらに、本軸の時空間的ヘテロ性や治療標的、臨床応用に向けた課題が議論されている。
summary_en: This review outlines the potential role of the NETs-cGAS-STING axis in driving neuroinflammation and immunothrombosis following ischemic stroke. NET-derived extracellular DNA is proposed to activate microglial cGAS-STING signaling, which in turn promotes neutrophil recruitment and secondary NET formation in a feed-forward loop. The article further discusses the spatiotemporal heterogeneity of this signaling axis and potential cell-specific therapeutic strategies.
key_finding_ja: NETsとcGAS-STING経路を介した好中球とミクログリアの相互作用が、虚血性脳卒中後の神経炎症を増幅する統合的フレームワークとして提唱された。
why_it_matters_ja: 脳卒中後の持続的炎症に対する新たな治療標的の概念を提供するが、臨床応用には病期や細胞特異性を考慮したさらなる検証が必要である。

title: Metabolic Reprogramming-Driven Neuroimmunoregulation: Key Mechanisms and Therapeutic Opportunities and Challenges in Central Nervous System Disorders.
abstract: Central nervous system (CNS) disorders are fundamentally linked to metabolic dysregulation within immune and glial cells. This review provides a systematic synthesis of immunometabolic reprogramming-encompassing glucose, lipid, and amino acid metabolism, and oxidative phosphorylation-in CNS-resident microglia, immunomodulatory astrocytes, and peripherally infiltrating immune cells (T cells, B cells, and neutrophils) across Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, multiple sclerosis, and ischemic stroke. Critically, rather than presenting all reported metabolic alterations as equivalently established, we introduce an evidence-transparency framework that systematically distinguishes the nature of supporting data-ranging from direct metabolic flux measurements (Seahorse, isotope tracing, lipidomics) and molecular correlates, to genetic/pharmacological perturbations, human tissue validation, and model-specific observations-enabling readers to independently assess the strength of each major conclusion. We further delineate aging as an active analytical dimension, demonstrating how age-related changes in mitochondrial quality control, lipid handling, redox buffering, and glial-immune crosstalk establish a permissive baseline that modifies disease-specific reprogramming trajectories. By integrating analyses of intercellular crosstalk, neuroinflammation, blood-brain barrier integrity, and oxidative stress, we illustrate both convergent and divergent metabolic mechanisms across diseases. Finally, we critically assess therapeutic strategies targeting immunometabolism, emphasizing shared translational obstacles including target selectivity, blood-brain barrier penetration, stage-dependent efficacy, and the inherent challenge of pathway pleiotropy. This review provides a conceptually grounded framework for interpreting immunometabolic evidence, navigating the gap between correlative findings and causal mechanisms, and guiding future hypothesis-driven therapeutic design for CNS disorders.
authors: Li N, Wu Y, Feng H, Jian X, Yang Z, Wang X, Li X, Yin Y, Long Y.
screening_reason: The review focuses on immunometabolic reprogramming of glial and immune cells as a central mechanism of neuroimmunoregulation in CNS disorders.
summary_ja: 中枢神経系疾患におけるミクログリア、アストロサイト、末梢浸潤免疫細胞の代謝リプログラミングと神経免疫調節に関する総説である。ブドウ糖、脂質、アミノ酸代謝および酸化燐酸化の変動を整理し、実験データのエビデンスレベルを客観的に評価する枠組みを提示している。また、加齢に伴うミトコンドリア品質管理や酸化ストレスの変化が疾患病態に与える影響についても解析している。さらに、免疫代謝を標的とした創薬における標的選択性や血液脳関門透過性などの課題を議論している。
summary_en: This review synthesizes immunometabolic reprogramming in resident glia and infiltrating immune cells across various central nervous system disorders. It establishes an evidence-transparency framework to evaluate metabolic findings while highlighting aging as a key factor modulating disease trajectories. Additionally, the authors discuss current translational challenges and therapeutic opportunities in targeting immunometabolism for neurological diseases.
key_finding_ja: 中枢神経系疾患における神経免疫応答と代謝リプログラミングの機序を整理し、エビデンス評価枠組みと治療開発上の課題を提示した。
why_it_matters_ja: 代謝標的型治療の設計や、観察データと因果関係の乖離を埋めるための体系的な概念的基盤を提供する。

title: Nonhistone Post-translational Modifications as Integrative Signaling Networks in Podocyte Injury and Glomerular Disease.
abstract: Podocytes are key structural components of the glomerular filtration barrier and are essential for maintaining selective protein filtration. Podocyte dysfunction is closely associated with proteinuria and the progression of glomerulosclerosis, constituting the common pathological basis of various chronic kidney diseases such as diabetic nephropathy and focal segmental glomerulosclerosis. While histone post-translational modifications have been extensively studied in podocyte biology, recent attention has shifted toward the regulatory roles of nonhistone post-translational modifications. By modulating protein stability, activity, localization, and interactions, these modifications participate in core biological processes such as apoptosis, cytoskeletal remodeling, inflammatory signaling, and metabolic reprogramming. Nevertheless, the strength of evidence is not uniform across post-translational modification categories. While some mechanisms have been directly demonstrated in podocytes, others are inferred mainly from broader kidney injury models or from studies in non-podocyte cell types. Accordingly, not all reported post-translational modification changes should be interpreted as equally well-established causal drivers of podocyte injury. This review focuses on the molecular regulatory networks and pathophysiological significance of major nonhistone post-translational modifications, including acetylation, phosphorylation, methylation, lactylation, ubiquitination, and SUMOylation. We further propose a hypothesis-generating and integrative conceptual model of podocyte deterioration, linking initiating pathological stimuli to stress transduction and downstream effector decompensation that may culminate in structural collapse. Importantly, this proposed cascade is not intended to represent a universally validated linear sequence or a definitive disease mechanism. Rather, it provides an organizing framework to generate testable hypotheses. We further highlight the therapeutic promise of targeting nonhistone post-translational modification pathways while acknowledging the considerable translational challenges that remain. By synthesizing the mechanistic landscape of nonhistone post-translational modifications, this review provides an integrated framework for advancing our understanding of podocytopathy pathogenesis and fostering the development of precision-targeted therapies.
authors: He Z, Jiang H, Tao S, Becker Y, Schroder P, Xiao J, Haller H, Ke G.
journal: Journal of the American Society of Nephrology : JASN
screening_reason: Central biological scope is nonhistone protein post-translational modifications (acetylation, phosphorylation, lactylation, ubiquitination, etc.) and their functional mechanisms.
summary_ja: 糸球体足細胞（ポドサイト）障害および糸球体疾患における非ヒストンタンパク質の翻訳後修飾（PTM）の役割をまとめたレビューである。アセチル化、リン酸化、メチル化、ラクチル化、ウビキチン化、SUMO化などの非ヒストンPTMが、ポドサイトのアポトーシスや骨格リモデリング、炎症シグナル伝達をどのように調節するかを解析している。研究レベルにおける証拠の強弱の違いを考慮し、病因に基づく概念モデルを提示して新たな仮説検証の枠組みを提供している。非ヒストンPTM経路を標的とした治療アプローチの可能性と、その臨床応用における実用上の課題についても言及している。
summary_en: This review focuses on the molecular regulatory networks of nonhistone post-translational modifications, including acetylation, phosphorylation, and ubiquitination, in podocyte injury and glomerular disease. These modifications regulate key biological processes such as cellular apoptosis, cytoskeletal remodeling, and inflammatory signaling. The authors propose an integrative conceptual model to guide future hypothesis testing while discussing the therapeutic potential and translational challenges of targeting these pathways.
key_finding_ja: 非ヒストンタンパク質の翻訳後修飾は、ポドサイト障害におけるアポトーシスや骨格リモデリングなどの分子伝達ネットワークを統合的に調節する。
why_it_matters_ja: 非ヒストン修飾ネットワークの解明は糸球体病変に対する精密な標的治療法の開発に繋がる可能性があるが、直接的な因果関係の証明には更なる研究が必要である。

title: Myokines, Microbiota, and Neuroinflammation: Physical Activity Modulates the Gut-Brain Axis.
abstract: Background Neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis are increasingly recognized as disorders influenced not only by intrinsic neural pathology but also by systemic physiological networks, including the gut-brain axis. Emerging evidence highlights physical activity as a potent modulator of this bidirectional communication system, with muscle-derived signals particularly myokines, metabolites, and extracellular vesicles playing a central role. Methods This narrative review synthesizes current knowledge on how exercise-induced molecular mediators influence gut microbiota composition, intestinal barrier integrity, immune signaling, and neuroinflammatory pathways. Findings were integrated across the disciplines of neuroscience, microbiology, and exercise physiology to evaluate mechanistic links between muscle-secreted factors and gut-mediated responses. Results Mechanistic links exist between muscle-secreted factors such as irisin, cathepsin B, BDNF-inducing pathways, and lactate with microbial metabolites including short-chain fatty acids. These interacting pathways demonstrate a combined impact on neuroprotection, synaptic plasticity, and the modulation of disease progression in neurodegenerative conditions. Conclusion Physical activity represents a promising non-pharmacological strategy for modulating the gut-brain axis in neurodegenerative conditions. Understanding the interplay between muscle-derived signals and gut-mediated pathways may open new avenues for targeted interventions aimed at slowing or preventing neurodegenerative decline.
authors: Yang Y, Yang Y, Tang Y, Yang W.
screening_reason: The review examines physical activity modulation of the gut-brain axis, gut microbiota composition, microbial metabolites, and neuroinflammation.
summary_ja: 神経変性疾患における運動駆動型の分子メディエーターと腸脳軸、および神経炎症の調節機構に関する文献を概括したナラティブレビューである。イリシンやカテプシンBなどの筋肉由来シグナルが、腸内細菌叢の組成や短鎖脂肪酸などの代謝物、腸管バリア機能に及ぼす影響を統合的に考察している。これらの相互作用経路が神経保護、シナプス可塑性、および神経炎症の修飾に寄与することが示されている。身体活動は非薬物療法として腸脳軸を介した神経変性疾患の進行抑制に寄与する可能性が提示されている。
summary_en: This review synthesizes current literature on how physical activity and muscle-derived signals, such as myokines and lactate, modulate the gut-brain axis and neuroinflammation in neurodegenerative diseases. Interactions between exercise-induced factors and microbial metabolites like short-chain fatty acids play a critical role in neuroprotection and immune signaling. Physical activity thus represents a promising non-pharmacological strategy targeting systemic physiological networks to slow neurodegenerative decline.
key_finding_ja: 運動によって分泌されるマイオカインなどの筋肉由来因子は、腸内細菌叢とその代謝物を介して神経炎症や神経保護に複合的な影響を与える。
why_it_matters_ja: 筋肉と腸内細菌叢、神経系の相互作用メカニズムの解明は、神経変性疾患に対する非薬物的な予防・治療介入手法の開発に寄与する可能性がある。

title: Investigating Gut Homeostasis in Stray Animals Across Different Air Pollution Zones.
abstract: Areas previously fulfilling air quality targets may face increased pressure to reevaluate due to stricter criteria. The gut homeostasis of stray animals may serve as a sensitive indicator of air pollution levels, yet previous research has primarily focused on model organisms. This cross-sectional study employed 16S rRNA sequencing and non-targeted metabolomics to assess changes in gut microbiota and metabolites across stray cat fecal samples from three air pollution zones in a coal-based industrial region in northern China-Polluted Zone 1 (DS), Polluted Zone 2 (WC), and Clean Zone (ZB). Air quality data confirmed significantly higher PM 2.5, SO 2 , CO, and NO 2 concentrations in polluted zones. The clean zone exhibited the highest gut microbial α-diversity, while polluted zones showed significantly lower diversity. Fecal metabolomic profiling identified a high-confidence subset of differentially abundant metabolites (DAMs). The transition from clean to polluted zones was associated with more pronounced biological remodeling than between polluted sites, suggesting a potential metabolic threshold effect. Lipids and lipid-like molecules represented the most disrupted superclass, with polluted cohorts showing altered bile acid profiles and accumulation of exogenous chemical remnants. Key neuroactive pathways-specifically retrograde endocannabinoid signaling and glutamatergic synapse-were consistently enriched among DAMs in polluted environments, reflecting localized remodeling of the host metabolic network. These findings suggest that air pollution exposure is associated with potential systemic health effects extending from the gut to the neuroendocrine level. This study provides evidence that environmental pollution gradients are independently associated with alterations in the feline gut microbiome-metabolome axis, highlighting the translational potential of urban stray cats as sentinel species within the One Health framework. Given the observational design, reported associations do not imply causation.
authors: Wang S, Cui L, Yue H.
screening_reason: The study examines alterations in the feline gut microbiome and fecal microbial metabolome in response to environmental air pollution.
summary_ja: 大気汚染が野生動物や野良動物の腸内恒常性に及ぼす影響についての理解は限定的です。本研究では、中国北部の異なる大気汚汚染ゾーンに生息する野良猫の糞便を用いて16S rRNA解析と代謝物解析を行いました。綺麗な地域と比較して汚染地域では腸内細菌叢のα多様性が低下し、胆汁酸や脂質代謝物、神経活性代謝経路に明確な変動が観察されました。
summary_en: Air pollution may alter host gut homeostasis, but evidence in non-model stray animals remains limited. This cross-sectional study examined fecal samples from stray cats across three air pollution zones in northern China using 16S rRNA sequencing and metabolomics. The results demonstrated lower microbial α-diversity and alterations in lipid metabolism, bile acid profiles, and neuroactive metabolites in cats exposed to higher air pollution.
key_finding_ja: 野良猫の腸内細菌叢と代謝物プロファイルは大気汚染の勾配に応じて変動しており、環境モニタリングの指標生物として有用である可能性が示された。
why_it_matters_ja: 本研究は横断的観察研究デザインであるため、大気汚染と腸内細菌叢の変化との間に直接的な因果関係があることを示すものではありません。

title: HDAC6 Inhibition Attenuates Early Brain Injury After Experimental Subarachnoid Hemorrhage and Suppresses Neuroinflammatory Responses.
abstract: Early brain injury (EBI) after subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) is closely associated with microglia-driven neuroinflammation, yet effective therapeutic strategies remain limited. Histone deacetylase 6 (HDAC6) has been implicated in neuroinflammatory regulation, but its role in microglial inflammatory activation after SAH remains unclear. In the present study, we investigated whether HDAC6 targeting attenuates SAH-induced EBI through modulation of microglia-associated neuroinflammation. A mouse prechiasmatic cistern blood-injection model of SAH and an Hb-stimulated primary microglia model were used to evaluate the effects of compound 13-7, an HDAC6-targeting inhibitor. We found that HDAC6 expression was significantly upregulated after SAH and was predominantly localized in microglia and neurons. Treatment with compound 13-7 increased α-tubulin acetylation in microglia, reduced brain edema, improved neurological deficits, and decreased neuronal apoptosis. In addition, compound 13-7 attenuated microglial inflammatory activation, reduced pro-inflammatory gene expression, decreased brain tissue levels of TNF-α, IFN-γ, and IL-6, and increased IL-4, IL-5, and IL-10 levels. In vitro, compound 13-7 protected neurons primarily through modulation of microglia-mediated inflammatory responses rather than by directly acting on neurons. Mechanistically, compound 13-7 reduced the p-P65/P65 ratio and suppressed NF-κB-related inflammatory gene expression in Hb-stimulated microglia. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that HDAC6 targeting attenuates SAH-induced EBI and improves neurological outcomes, at least partly by suppressing microglia-associated neuroinflammation and restoring inflammatory cytokine balance. Inhibition of NF-κB signaling may contribute to the anti-inflammatory effects of compound 13-7, highlighting HDAC6 as a potential therapeutic target for SAH-induced EBI.
authors: Zhang R, Hu J, Jiang Y, Jiang Y, Wang X, Chen Y, Zhang A, Tong X.
screening_reason: Mechanistic study demonstrating HDAC6 inhibition suppresses microglial inflammatory activation and neuroinflammation following subarachnoid hemorrhage.
summary_ja: くも膜下出血後の早期脳損傷にはミクログリアが主導する神経炎症が密接に関与しています。本研究ではHDAC6阻害剤であるcompound 13-7を用いてマウスSAHモデルおよび微小血管・神経細胞培養系での作用を検証しました。その結果、HDAC6阻害はα-tubulinのアセチル化を高め、脳浮腫や神経細胞死を減弱させるとともに、ミクログリアにおけるNF-κBシグナルの抑制を介して炎症性サイトカインの産生を抑えることが示されました。
summary_en: Subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) induces early brain injury (EBI) closely linked to microglial neuroinflammation. This study evaluated compound 13-7, an HDAC6 inhibitor, in mouse SAH and primary microglial models. Inhibiting HDAC6 increased α-tubulin acetylation, reduced brain edema and neuronal apoptosis, and suppressed microglial inflammatory activation via NF-κB signaling.
key_finding_ja: HDAC6阻害剤compound 13-7は、ミクログリアのNF-κBシグナル抑制を介して神経炎症を減弱させ、くも膜下出血後の早期脳損傷を軽減した。
why_it_matters_ja: 本研究成果は動物および細胞モデルでの知見であり、ヒトのくも膜下出血患者における安全性や有効性の解明にはさらなる臨床研究が必要です。

title: From association to mechanism: AA:DHA supplementation, the preterm gut microbiome, and retinopathy of prematurity.
abstract: Impact AA:DHA supplementation may be associated with selected taxonomic and inferred functional features of the gut microbiome in extremely preterm infants, but current evidence does not establish the microbiome as a mediator of reduced severe retinopathy of prematurity. Denser longitudinal sampling and detailed information on antibiotics, feeding, microbial function, and clinical events are needed to move from microbial associations towards causal mechanisms.
authors: Lamadrid-Figueroa H.
screening_reason: Evaluates the relationship between fatty acid supplementation, the preterm gut microbiome, and retinopathy of prematurity.
summary_ja: 本論文は、超未熟児におけるAA:DHAサプリメント摂取と腸内細菌叢および未熟児網膜症（ROP）との関連性について考察している。現在の知見では、AA:DHAの補給が特定の腸内細菌叢の特徴と関連している可能性が示されているが、腸内細菌叢が重症ROP軽減の仲介因子であるという因果関係は立証されていない。単なる相関から因果メカニズムの解明へと移行するためには、高頻度の縦断的サンプリングや、抗生剤使用、栄養法、菌叢機能、臨床イベントの詳細なデータ収集が必要であると結論付けられている。
summary_en: This article highlights that while AA:DHA supplementation in extremely preterm infants may correlate with specific gut microbiome features, current evidence does not establish the microbiome as a causal mediator of reduced severe retinopathy of prematurity. The authors emphasize that dense longitudinal sampling and detailed clinical and microbial data are required to establish true causal mechanisms.
key_finding_ja: 超未熟児におけるAA:DHA補給と腸内細菌叢の関連は観察されているものの、腸内細菌叢が重症未熟児網膜症の軽減を仲介するという因果関係は証明されていない。
why_it_matters_ja: 腸内細菌叢と疾患との関連において単なる相関を超えた因果メカニズムを解明することの重要性を提起している。

title: A Small-Molecule DEPTAC Rescues Cognitive Deficits by Targeted Dephosphorylation of Pathological Tau.
abstract: Accumulation of hyperphosphorylated Tau (p-Tau) is a central driver of neurodegeneration in Alzheimer's disease (AD). Addressing the limitations of current therapeutics, we developed TP2, a small-molecule DEPhosphorylation-TArgeting Chimera (DEPTAC). TP2 is engineered to physically tether endogenous PP2A to Tau, facilitating targeted dephosphorylation. Mechanistically, TP2 induces ternary complex formation and potently reduces p-Tau in neurons. Systemic administration of TP2 in distinct tauopathy mouse models (P301L and AAV-hTau-N368) significantly lowered brain p-Tau levels, oligomers, and neurofibrillary tangles without altering global PP2A activity. Crucially, by rebalancing the phosphorylation of Tau, TP2 restored Tau's physiological function, as evidenced by the preservation of neuronal morphology, synaptic integrity, and microtubule stability. TP2 also ameliorated the dysregulated neuroimmune microenvironment. Consequently, TP2 treatment robustly reversed cognitive deficits in multiple behavioral paradigms. These findings establish TP2 as a promising therapeutic candidate that targets upstream pathological phosphorylation to halt neurodegeneration and restore cognitive function.
authors: Sun F, Liu Y, Zhou Q, Hu Q, Wang W, Xiao Y, Su J, Liu G, Sun M, Chen L, Li H, Yang Y, Wang JZ.
screening_reason: Focuses on targeted dephosphorylation, a protein post-translational modification mechanism, to rescue Tau pathology.
summary_ja: アルツハイマー病における過剰リン酸化タウ（p-Tau）の蓄積に対し、内因性PP2Aをタウに物理的に結合させて脱リン酸化を促す化合物TP2を開発しました。タウオパチーマウスモデルへの投与により、全般的なPP2A活性を変えることなく脳内のp-Tau、タウオリゴマー、神経原線維変化が減少しました。さらに、神経元の形態やシナプスの完全性が保持され、行動評価における認知機能低下が改善しました。
summary_en: Researchers developed TP2, a small-molecule chimera designed to induce targeted dephosphorylation of hyperphosphorylated Tau by tethering it to PP2A. Systemic administration of TP2 in tauopathy mouse models significantly reduced pathological Tau species without altering global PP2A activity. This targeted modification preserved neuronal morphology and synaptic integrity, ultimately reversing cognitive deficits.
key_finding_ja: 標的脱リン酸化化合物TP2の投与により、タウオパチーマウスの脳内リン酸化タウが減少し認知機能が回復した。
why_it_matters_ja: 病理的リン酸化という翻訳後修飾を標的とした治療法は、アルツハイマー病などの神経変性疾患に対する新たな戦略となる可能性があります。

title: Microbiome-Driven Therapeutic Strategies for Type 2 Diabetes: A Systematic Review of Microbiota Modulation, Glycaemic Outcomes, and Transplantation.
abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) arises from the body's ineffective use or production of insulin. Recent research highlights the significant role of the gut microbiome in metabolism and immunity, indicating that microbial dysbiosis may be associated with T2DM development. This systematic review will explore the link between gut dysbiosis and Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (T2DM), assess the impact of microbially-targeted therapies such as probiotics, prebiotics, dietary changes, and fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) on glycaemic and metabolic outcomes in adults with T2DM, and determine if clinical trials validate the application of these therapies for T2DM treatment. An extensive literature search was conducted using PubMed up to January 2024, adhering to PRISMA 2020 guidelines, to identify eligible studies. The studies included were randomized controlled trials or observational studies reporting measurable outcomes related to metabolic health in adults aged 18 and older. A total of 25 studies show that individuals with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (T2DM) have lower gut microbial diversity, featuring fewer butyrate-producing bacteria and more inflammation-related bacteria. Probiotic supplementation and dietary fiber intake significantly improve hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) levels and insulin sensitivity in T2DM patients. Gut microbiota dysbiosis is linked to Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (T2DM), suggesting that the gut microbiome could be a therapeutic focus. However, while interventions like dietary changes, probiotics, and fecal microbiota transplantation show potential, current evidence does not support their routine clinical application. Recommendations for microbiome interventions should rely on strong evidence from effective longitudinal clinical trials verifying both efficacy and safety.
authors: Haneesh M, Amalraj S, Anusha G, Karthick V, Poongavanam SS, Thamarai R.
screening_reason: This systematic review analyzes gut microbiome dysbiosis and microbiota-targeted interventions in type 2 diabetes mellitus.
summary_ja: 2型糖尿病（T2DM）患者における腸内細菌叢の乱れとマイクロバイオームを標的とした治療戦略に関する系統的レビューである。25件の研究を解析した結果、T2DM患者では腸内細菌の多様性が低下し、酪酸産生菌が減少する一方で炎症関連菌が増加していることが確認された。プロバイオティクス摂取や食物繊維の導入により、HbA1cレベルやインスリン感受性の改善が示された。しかし、現時点では日常的な臨床応用を支持する十分な証拠は確立されておらず、更なる縦断的臨床試験が必要であると結論付けられている。
summary_en: This systematic review evaluated 25 studies examining the link between gut microbiota dysbiosis and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). The analysis showed that patients with T2DM exhibit lower microbial diversity, reduced levels of butyrate-producing bacteria, and increased numbers of inflammation-associated species. While probiotic supplementation and dietary fiber significantly improved HbA1c and insulin sensitivity, current evidence remains insufficient to support their routine clinical application.
key_finding_ja: 2型糖尿病患者では腸内細菌の多様性低下と酪酸産生菌の減少が認められ、プロバイオティクスや食物繊維の補給によりHbA1cおよびインスリン感受性が改善した。
why_it_matters_ja: 腸内細菌叢を標的とした介入は2型糖尿病の新たな治療戦略として期待されるが、日常的な臨床導入には更なる検証が必要である。

title: LECT2-RPS27A interaction involving Lys48 attenuates neuroinflammation in diabetic retinopathy.
abstract: Aims/hypothesis Leukocyte cell-derived chemotaxin 2 (LECT2), a newly discovered hepatokine involved in immunomodulation and inflammatory processes, has recently been implicated in diabetic retinopathy pathogenesis. However, the specific role and mechanism of LECT2 in diabetic retinopathy remain largely unclear. Methods A publicly available liquid biopsy proteomics dataset was reanalysed and validated using retinal samples from individuals with diabetic retinopathy. A LECT2-knockdown (Lect2 +/- ) mouse model of diabetic retinopathy was established to evaluate the role of LECT2 in vivo. Retinal pathology was assessed by Periodic Acid-Schiff staining and H&E staining, and LECT2 expression was assessed by western blotting. In parallel, a high glucose (HG)-induced human Müller cell model was used to investigate the subcellular localisation and functional effects of LECT2. LECT2 expression and inflammatory signalling were analysed following LECT2 knockdown or overexpression, and its nucleus-cytoplasm distribution was examined by fractionation assays. The interaction between LECT2 and ribosomal protein S27a (RPS27A) was characterised by immunoprecipitation-MS, co-immunoprecipitation, molecular docking and split-GFP assays, followed by RPS27A silencing to assess its effects on inflammatory protein expression. Results Proteomic reanalysis of proliferative diabetic retinopathy liquid biopsy data identified 1479 upregulated proteins, with chemotaxis among the most significantly enriched Gene Ontology terms (false discovery rate +/- mice, LECT2 deficiency aggravated retinal microvascular injury and inflammatory responses. LECT2 was predominantly expressed in retinal Müller cells, implicating it in glia-associated retinal inflammation. In HG-treated human retinal Müller cells, RPS27A was identified as a downstream target of LECT2 and was upregulated under hyperglycaemic conditions. Mechanistically, HG stimulation increased the expression and nuclear accumulation of both LECT2 and RPS27A. LECT2 interacted with RPS27A at the Lys48 site, promoting its nuclear retention and limiting its cytoplasmic translocation. This, in turn, inhibited IκBα ubiquitination and degradation, thereby suppressing NF-κB-driven inflammatory signalling. Conclusions/interpretation Taken together, our studies indicated the protective role of LECT2 in diabetes-induced dysfunction of retinal Müller cells, supporting the feasibility of targeting LECT2 in the management of diabetic inflammation and microvasculopathy.
authors: Liu Z, Yin H, Zhu K, Shao L, Wang Y, Yuan Y, Zhang J, Lin S, Wang Q, Jin L, Chen J, Liu Q, He W, Ying M, Zhang L.
screening_reason: The study uncovers a mechanism where LECT2 interaction at Lys48 on RPS27A inhibits IkappaBalpha ubiquitination, suppressing glial-mediated neuroinflammation.
summary_ja: ヘパトカインであるLECT2は糖尿病網膜症に関与することが知られていますが、その機序は不明でした。本研究では、糖尿病網膜症モデルマウスおよび高糖刺激ヒトミューラー細胞を用いて機能解析を実施しました。LECT2はRPS27AのLys48部位で直接相互作用して核内留置を促し、IκBαのユビキチン化と分解を抑えることで、NF-κBを介した網膜神経炎症を抑制することが明らかになりました。
summary_en: LECT2 is a hepatokine involved in diabetic retinopathy, but its precise target mechanisms remain unclear. Using diabetic retinopathy mouse models and high-glucose-treated human Müller cells, researchers discovered that LECT2 binds to RPS27A at the Lys48 site. This interaction promotes nuclear retention of RPS27A, inhibiting IκBα ubiquitination and degradation and thereby attenuating NF-κB-driven neuroinflammation.
key_finding_ja: LECT2はRPS27AのLys48部位での結合を介してIκBαのユビキチン化と分解を阻害し、糖尿病網膜症における神経炎症を軽減させる。
why_it_matters_ja: 本研究は培養細胞および動物モデルにおける分子機序の解明であり、ヒトの糖尿病性微小血管症治療に直結させるには臨床試験による評価が必要です。

title: K ATP channel functional remodeling is associated with neuroinflammatory and dopaminergic alterations under metabolic stress in female mice.
abstract: Metabolic stress and neuroinflammation are associated with depression, but the mechanisms connecting peripheral metabolic dysfunction to reward-related circuit alterations remain incompletely understood. ATP-sensitive potassium (K ATP ) channels couple cellular energy state to neuronal excitability and may link metabolic and neuroimmune signaling. Here, we used female mice exposed to post-weaning isolation combined with a high-fat diet to model convergent psychosocial and metabolic stress. We tested whether K ATP channel modulation is associated with behavioral, inflammatory, and dopaminergic-marker changes under this combined stress condition. Peripheral K ATP channel modulation was achieved by interscapular brown adipose tissue infusion of glibenclamide, and dopaminergic neuron-specific Kir6.2 conditional knockout mice were used to assess the contribution of neuronal K ATP channel signaling. Combined stress induced obesity, hyperglycemia, depression-like behavioral alterations, peripheral cytokine imbalance, increased inflammatory markers, and reduced dopaminergic activity markers in the mesolimbic pathway. Glibenclamide improved glucose tolerance, attenuated stress-associated behavioral and inflammatory-marker changes, and increased Fos expression under stress conditions, while enhancing SUR1 maturation and surface localization. Kir6.2 deletion attenuated stress-associated behavioral alterations and reduced nucleus accumbens Iba1-positive cell accumulation, whereas effects on ventral tegmental area tyrosine hydroxylase-positive cell density were more modest. Together, these findings support K ATP channel functional state as a candidate link between metabolic stress, neuroimmune alterations, and dopaminergic circuit adaptations in female mice, and suggest K ATP c hannel modulation as a potential therapeutic strategy for metabolic-associated depression.
authors: Chen CL, Li PY, Tsai HY, Chen JF, Wang YC, Lin YC, Lai YS, Chen SR, Kuo YM, Tzeng SF, Chen PS, Yang SB, Lin CH, Chen PC.
screening_reason: The study focuses on ATP-sensitive potassium channel signaling linking metabolic stress with neuroimmune and neuroinflammatory responses.
summary_ja: 代謝ストレスと神経炎症はうつ病に関与しますが、両者をつなぐ詳細なメカニズムは未解明です。本研究では、隔離飼育と高脂肪食を組み合わせた複合ストレスを負荷したメスマウスを用いてK ATPチャネルの役割を解析しました。K ATPチャネルの薬理学的修飾や神経細胞特異的Kir6.2欠損により、ストレス下での行動異常や中枢炎症指標、中脳辺縁系ドーパミン指標の変化が抑えられることが確認されました。
summary_en: Metabolic stress and neuroinflammation are implicated in depression, but the underlying bridging mechanisms remain poorly understood. Using a female mouse model of combined psychosocial and metabolic stress, this study tested the role of ATP-sensitive potassium (K ATP) channels. Pharmacological modulation of K ATP channels or dopaminergic Kir6.2 deletion attenuated stress-induced behavioral alterations and neuroimmune inflammatory markers.
key_finding_ja: K ATPチャネルの機能状態は、代謝ストレス、中枢免疫系の変化、およびドーパミン神経回路の適応的変動を仲介する分子リンクである可能性が示された。
why_it_matters_ja: 本知見は雌マウスモデルで得られた実験結果に基づくものであり、ヒトの代謝性うつ病に対する治療法開発には慎重な検証が必要です。

title: Differential consequences of traumatic brain injury in male rat hippocampus hemispheres and the beneficial effect of neuropeptide Y.
abstract: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) initiates a complex cascade of secondary injury mechanisms, including neurovascular dysfunction, neuroinflammation, and glial activation, which progressively contribute to long-term neurological deficits. Although the primary mechanical insult is typically unilateral, secondary pathological processes can extend beyond the impact site. However, the spatiotemporal evolution of these bilateral alterations remains poorly understood. Neuropeptide Y (NPY) is an endogenous neuromodulator with anti-inflammatory and neuroprotective properties, making it a promising candidate for limiting secondary brain injury. Here, we characterized the bilateral hippocampal response to experimental TBI and evaluated whether early intranasal NPY administration post-TBI attenuates neurovascular and neuroinflammatory alterations while improving behavioral outcomes. Male Sprague-Dawley rats were subjected to a closed-head weight-drop model of TBI and treated intranasally with NPY (100 μg/animal) or vehicle 30 min after injury. Molecular, histological, and behavioral analyses were performed 48 h and 7 days post-injury. We concluded that TBI induced distinct spatiotemporal pathological responses in the hippocampi. The ipsilateral hippocampus exhibited early blood-brain barrier (BBB) disruption and astrocytic alterations, whereas the contralateral hippocampus developed a more pronounced and sustained inflammatory response characterized by microglial activation and increased expression of inflammatory and endothelial activation markers. Early intranasal NPY administration attenuated these bilateral pathological alterations by preserving BBB integrity, reducing neuroinflammatory responses, and normalizing glial morphology. These neurobiological effects were accompanied by improvements in spatial working memory and anxiety-related behaviors. Collectively, our findings demonstrate that unilateral TBI induces distinct bilateral secondary injury responses within the hippocampus and identify early intranasal NPY administration as a promising strategy. Further investigation is warranted to clarify the underlying mechanisms and establish the long-term therapeutic potential of NPY.
authors: Leitão RA, Alves JL, Bernardo AL, Mota-Pinto A, Silva AP.
screening_reason: The central topic is the attenuation of microglial activation and post-traumatic neuroinflammation by early neuropeptide Y treatment.
summary_ja: ラットモデルを用いた片側性頭部外傷（TBI）後の両側海馬における病理学的変化と、ニューロペプチドY（NPY）の経鼻投与の効果が調べられた。TBI後、障害と同側の海馬では早期の血液脳関門破綻とアストロサイトの変化が観察された一方、対側の海馬ではミクログリア活性化を伴う持続的な炎症反応が認められた。損傷30分後のNPY経鼻投与は、血液脳関門の透過性を保ち、両側性の神経炎症および膠細胞の変化を抑えた。これらの作用に伴い、空間作業記憶の低下および不安様行動の増悪が改善された。
summary_en: In a male rat model of traumatic brain injury (TBI), unilateral injury produced distinct bilateral pathological patterns in the hippocampus, with early blood-brain barrier disruption ipsilaterally and sustained neuroinflammation contralaterally. Early intranasal administration of neuropeptide Y (NPY) attenuated these bilateral pathological alterations by preserving blood-brain barrier integrity and suppressing neuroinflammatory responses. These neurobiological effects were accompanied by improvements in spatial working memory and anxiety-related behaviors.
key_finding_ja: 片側性TBIは海馬の両側で異なる時空間的病理反応を引き起こすが、損傷後の早期NPY経鼻投与により血液脳関門の維持、神経炎症の抑制、および行動障害の改善が認められた。
why_it_matters_ja: 外傷性脳損傷後の広範な二次的障害を軽減するための治療法として、早期の経鼻NPY投与が有効な戦略となる可能性が期待される。

title: Deletion of RGS5 attenuates high-fat diet-induced cerebrovascular pathology and associated spatial memory deficits.
abstract: Diet-induced metabolic dysregulation is associated with cerebral microvascular pathology contributing to cognitive decline and vascular dementia. These alterations include blood-brain barrier (BBB) leakage, pericyte dysfunction, aberrant angiogenesis, and perivascular neuroinflammation. Restoration of BBB integrity has been achieved in other conditions by targeting pericytes, for example through knockout of Regulator of G-protein Signaling 5 (RGS5), a sensor protein for hypoxia and oxidative stress highly enriched in these cells. It remains unclear whether deletion of RGS5 can provide vascular protection in conditions of chronic metabolic stress and prevent cognitive impairment despite ongoing metabolic dysfunction. We used constitutional RGS5 knockout (KO) mice and wildtype (WT) controls fed a standard or high-fat diet (HFD) for 23 weeks to induce metabolic dysfunction, confirmed by weight gain, insulinemia, and impaired glucose tolerance. BBB leakage, vascular pathology (vessel density, branching, pericyte density and coverage), microglial activation and microglia-capillary interactions were analyzed using immunohistochemistry. Spatial memory was evaluated using the novel object location test. HFD induced obesity, glucose intolerance and insulin resistance in all mice. In WT but not RGS5-KO mice, HFD caused BBB leakage, immature angiogenesis, and pericyte activation. RGS5 deletion also prevented microglial activation and enhanced interactions between resting microglia and striatal vessels. Importantly, HFD-induced impairment of spatial memory was prevented in KO mice. These data suggest that deletion of RGS5 preserves BBB integrity, maintains microvascular homeostasis, reduces neuroinflammation, and ameliorates memory decline in diet-induced metabolic dysfunction. These findings highlight RGS5 as potential therapeutic target and emphasize microvascular dysfunction as contributor to HFD-induced cognitive decline.
authors: Elabi OF, Tiwari S, Garcia-Serrano AM, Carlsson R, Polo CN, Fonseca-Fonseca LA, Duarte JMN, Paul G.
screening_reason: The paper investigates perivascular neuroinflammation, microglial activation, and blood-brain barrier integrity in a high-fat diet model.
summary_ja: 高脂肪食により誘発される代謝異常に伴う脳微小血管病変および認知機能低下におけるRGS5の役割を評価するため、RGS5欠損マウスを用いた実験が行われた。高脂肪食を23週間給餌した野生型マウスでは、血液脳関門の漏出、未熟な血管新生、ペリサイト活性化、およびミクログリアの活性化が見られた。一方、RGS5欠損マウスではこれらの脳血管病変および神経炎症が抑制され、空間記憶障害の発生が防がれた。これらの結果は、RGS5の欠損が代謝異常下においても血管保護作用と神経炎症抑制効果をもたらすことを示している。
summary_en: In mice fed a high-fat diet, deletion of Regulator of G-protein Signaling 5 (RGS5) preserved blood-brain barrier integrity and microvascular homeostasis while suppressing microglial activation. Additionally, RGS5 knockout prevented high-fat diet-induced spatial memory deficits despite persistent systemic metabolic dysfunction. These results highlight RGS5 as a potential target to mitigate cerebrovascular pathology and cognitive decline related to metabolic stress.
key_finding_ja: 高脂肪食を給餌したマウスにおいて、RGS5の欠損は血液脳関門の破綻やミクログリア活性化などの脳血管病変を抑制し、空間記憶障害の発生を防止した。
why_it_matters_ja: 代謝異常に伴う血管性認知症や認知機能低下に対する治療標的として、RGS5および脳微小血管病変の制御が有望である可能性が示唆される。

title: Brain Tissue-Derived Exosomal Proteomics Identifies Chemotaxis-Associated Protein Changes After Traumatic Brain Injury: An Exploratory Hippocampal Transcriptomic Comparison.
abstract: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) involves both primary and secondary pathological processes, including hemorrhage, ischemia, edema, and neuroinflammation. Although tissue-derived exosomes have emerged as important mediators of intercellular communication within local tissue microenvironments, their role in TBI-associated inflammatory responses remains incompletely understood. This study integrated brain tissue-derived exosomal proteomics with publicly available hippocampal transcriptomic data to investigate the potential association between tissue-derived exosomes and chemotaxis-related inflammatory responses after TBI. Brain tissue-derived exosomes were isolated, characterized, and subjected to label-free proteomic analysis. Public hippocampal transcriptomic data from GSE173975 were analyzed, and differentially expressed proteins (DEPs) and genes (DEGs) were identified from the exosomal proteomic and transcriptomic datasets, respectively. Functional enrichment, co-enrichment, and protein-protein interaction network analyses were performed, followed by quantitative real-time PCR, exosomal western blotting, and Transwell migration assays for validation and functional assessment. In total, 190 DEPs and 465 DEGs were identified. Co-enrichment analyses highlighted immune- and inflammation-related processes, particularly chemotaxis-related processes and chemokine signaling. LGALS3 and ITGB2 were increased at the exosomal protein level in brain tissue-derived exosomes from TBI rats and also showed increased hippocampal mRNA expression, whereas CCL2, CCL3, and CCR5 were upregulated at the hippocampal mRNA level. Functionally, TBI-derived exosomes enhanced BV2 microglial migration in vitro. Overall, these findings suggest that injury-associated brain tissue-derived exosomes may be associated with chemotaxis-related inflammatory and pro-migratory responses after TBI.
authors: Chen WC, Chen XL, Lin CY, Huang YZ, He HF, Zhou YL, Liu YB.
screening_reason: The research directly investigates traumatic brain injury-induced neuroinflammation, exosomal signaling, and microglial chemotactic migration.
summary_ja: 外傷性脳損傷（TBI）後の局所微小環境における炎症反応を解明するため、ラットの脳組織由来エキソソームプロテオミクスと海馬トランスクリプトミクスを統合解析しました。解析により、TBI群のエキソソームにおいてLGALS3やITGB2などの走化性関連タンパク質の増加が確認されました。インビトロ実験では、TBI由来エキソソームがBV2ミクログリアの細胞遊走を促進することが確認されました。
summary_en: Researchers integrated brain tissue-derived exosomal proteomics and hippocampal transcriptomics from a rat traumatic brain injury model to investigate post-injury inflammatory responses. They identified chemotaxis-related proteins, such as LGALS3 and ITGB2, enriched in exosomes following brain injury. Functional assays further demonstrated that TBI-derived exosomes enhanced microglial cell migration in vitro.
key_finding_ja: 外傷性脳損傷後に脳組織から分泌されるエキソソームが走化性関連タンパク質を含み、ミクログリアの遊走を促進することが示された。
why_it_matters_ja: 脳損傷後のエキソソームを介した神経炎症制御機構の理解が進むことで、脳創傷における炎症抑制の新たな治療標的同定につながる可能性があります。

title: Associations of smoking, aging, and their interplay with the gut microbiome and chronic disease risk profiles.
abstract: Introduction Smoking and aging are both linked to chronic disease and gut microbiome, but their joint relationship with microbiome composition remains uncharacterized. This study examined the overlap between smoking- and age-associated gut microbial signals and their associations with cardiovascular diseases. Methods We analyzed 6676 participants from a filtered project-specific metadata subset from the Guangdong Gut Microbiome Project together with the public GGMP OTU table. Associations of smoking phenotypes and aging with gut microbiota were examined using multivariable linear models. Additional sensitivity analyses were performed in males only, and robustness analyses were repeated at the family and genus levels. Results We identified 222 OTUs associated with first-hand smoking and 117 OTUs associated with second-hand smoke exposure. Among never smokers, age was associated with 330 OTUs. Eighty-five OTUs overlapped between smoking- and age-associated signals. Differences in the abundance of these OTU groups between never smokers and daily smokers were more pronounced in younger than older age strata. The smoking- and age-related OTU groups were associated with several cardiometabolic markers, and mediation analysis suggested that systolic blood pressure may partly account for the association between this overlapping microbial signal and ASCVD risk score. In a male-only sensitivity analysis, the central smoking-aging microbial signal remained directionally consistent. Family- and genus-level robustness analyses also supported persistence of selected associations. Conclusions In this cross-sectional secondary analysis, smoking and aging were associated with overlapping gut microbiome patterns, with stronger smoking-related deviations in younger adults. These findings support future longitudinal studies of microbiome-linked cardiovascular risk in smoking-exposed populations.
authors: Bao Z, Yang Z, Sun R, Meng R, Wu W, Li MD.
journal: Nicotine & tobacco research : official journal of the Society for Research on Nicotine and Tobacco
screening_reason: The study centers on mapping gut microbiome composition shifts associated with smoking and aging and their relationship to cardiovascular risk.
summary_ja: Guangdong Gut Microbiome Projectのデータ（6,676名）を用いて、喫煙と加齢が腸内細菌叢に与える重複した影響を解析しました。喫煙関連および加齢関連のOTUのうち85個が重複しており、日常喫煙による菌叢の偏りは高齢層よりも若年層でより著しいことが判明しました。また、この重複する微生物シグナルは心血管代謝マーカーやASCVDリスクスコアと関連しており、収縮期血圧がその媒介因子の一部である可能性が示唆されました。
summary_en: Analyzing 6,676 participants from a large microbiome project, researchers evaluated overlapping gut microbial signatures associated with smoking and aging. They identified 85 operational taxonomic units shared between smoking- and age-associated signals, with more pronounced smoking-related differences observed in younger age strata. Mediation analysis suggested that blood pressure may partially account for the relationship between this microbial signal and cardiovascular risk.
key_finding_ja: 喫煙と加齢は重複する腸内細菌叢パターンと関連しており、若年者において喫煙に伴う菌叢変化がより顕著であった。
why_it_matters_ja: 喫煙と加齢に共通する菌叢シグナルが心血管リスクに関連することを示す結果であり、環境要因と加齢が微細生態系に与える影響の解明に繋がります。

title: ADP-ribosylation: An emerging regulator of the epigenome.
abstract: ADP-ribosylation (ADPRylation) is a post-translational modification best known for its roles in DNA damage responses and cytoplasmic signaling, but it also serves important functions in epigenome regulation. In the nucleus, ADPRylation modulates chromatin structure and gene expression through the coordinated modification of histones and chromatin-associated proteins. Although poly(ADP-ribosyl)ation (PARylation) has dominated the field, particularly as therapeutic targets in DNA repair deficient malignancies, a gap remains in our understanding of how mono(ADP-ribosyl)ation (MARylation)-mediated by mono(ADP-ribosyl) transferases (MARTs)-functions as a discrete, site-specific epigenomic mark. Nuclear MART-mediated ADPRylation modulates the activity, localization, and complex assembly of epigenomic enzymes, and directly modifies histones to influence chromatin accessibility and transcriptional dynamics. These reversible modifications intersect with canonical epigenomic marks, enabling rapid, context-dependent control of gene expression. Emerging studies further implicate dysregulated nuclear ADPRylation in cancer, where altered MARylation of chromatin regulators and transcription factors contributes to aberrant gene expression programs and may represent a novel class of therapeutic vulnerabilities. In this review, we synthesize emerging insights into nuclear ADPRylation, with a focus on MART-mediated regulation of histones and chromatin enzymes, and discuss how this regulatory layer expands current models of epigenomic control in physiology and how its alterations drive oncogenesis, offering novel, nonsynthetically lethal avenues for targeted cancer therapy.
authors: Camacho CV, Liu C, Kraus WL.
screening_reason: Focuses entirely on the mechanisms and biological roles of ADP-ribosylation as a protein post-translational modification.
summary_ja: 本総説では、翻訳後修飾の一種であるADPリボシル化（ADPRylation）がエピゲノムやクロマチン構造を調節する役割について解説しています。特にモノADPリボシル化転移酵素（MART）を介したモノADPリボシル化（MARylation）が、ヒストンやクロマチン関連酵素の機能や局在を動的に変化させるメカニズムに焦点を当てています。さらに、がんにおける核内ADPリボシル化の異常と、それを標的とした新たな治療法への応用可能性を議論しています。
summary_en: This review highlights the emerging role of nuclear ADP-ribosylation as a key post-translational modification regulating the epigenome and chromatin structure. It focuses on mono(ADP-ribosyl)ation mediated by MARTs and its capacity to modulate histones and chromatin enzymes. The authors also discuss how dysregulated ADP-ribosylation contributes to oncogenesis and provides potential novel therapeutic targets.
key_finding_ja: モノADPリボシル化を中心とする核内ADPリボシル化が、クロマチン構造と遺伝子発現を精密に調節する重要な翻訳後修飾層であることが提示された。
why_it_matters_ja: ADPリボシル化によるエピゲノム制御機構の解明は、がん治療における新たな分子標的の同定につながる可能性があります。

title: PIWI-piRNA Axis in Epilepsy: Bridging Epigenetic Regulation, Neuroinflammation, and Neuronal Excitability.
abstract: Epilepsy is a chronic neurological disorder characterized by recurrent seizures, neuroinflammation, and epigenetic instability, with around one-third of patients experiencing drug-resistant epilepsy. While ion channels and neurotransmitter imbalances have been thoroughly examined in relation to epilepsy, the significance of piRNAs and their interaction with PIWI proteins in gene regulation, transposon silencing, and inflammatory signaling inside the epileptic brain is gaining recognition. This summary encapsulates the existing understanding of piRNA synthesis, the epigenetic control through PIWI-piRNA interactions, and their novel roles in epileptogenesis. PIWI-piRNA complexes target highly expressed genomic areas, such as LINE-1 retrotransposons, and mute them by recruiting chromatin modifiers such DNMT3A and H3K9 methyltransferase complexes, therefore influencing genome stability and neuronal excitability. Additionally, piRNAs initiate pathways associated with neuroinflammation, including the activation of the Toll-like receptor-4/NF-kB signaling pathway and the NLRP3 inflammasome, and indirectly influence GABAergic homeostasis through interactions with the extensive noncoding RNA regulatory network. Targeted modulation of kainic acid, pilocarpine, and hereditary epilepsy models has been documented to provide decreases in seizure load; however, the extent of this effect varies among the models and modulation techniques employed. The review critically evaluates emerging therapeutic strategies, including AAV9 vectors, lipid nanoparticles, exosome-based delivery systems, and antisense oligonucleotides, along with their associated challenges such as blood-brain barrier penetration, off-target effects, immune activation, and long-term safety. In conclusion, the PIWI-piRNA axis represents a potential yet nascent domain for biomarker creation and disease modulation in epilepsy.
authors: Shyam M, Rashmi R, Sharma V, Venkatesh R, Jain A, G Y, Gopalakrishnan AV, Srirangan P, Prince SE.
screening_reason: Examines the PIWI-piRNA axis in modulating neuroinflammatory pathways (TLR4/NF-kB and NLRP3) in the context of epilepsy.
summary_ja: てんかんの病態生理におけるPIWI-piRNA軸のエピジェネティクス修飾、神経炎症、および神経興奮性に対する役割を整理したレビューである。PIWI-piRNA複合体によるエピジェネティック制御がレトロトランスポゾンをサイレンシングし、ゲノム安定性と神経興奮性に影響を与えるメカニズムが論じられている。さらに、piRNAがTLR4/NF-κB経路やNLRP3インフラマソームを介して神経炎症を誘導・修飾する機構や、GABA作動性ホームオスタシスへの関与を解説している。AAV9や脂質ナノ粒子、核酸医薬を用いた治療応用への課題と展望についても議論されている。
summary_en: This review highlights the role of the PIWI-piRNA axis in epilepsy, bridging epigenetic gene regulation, neuroinflammation, and neuronal excitability. PIWI-piRNA complexes target retrotransposons to influence genome stability while modulating inflammatory signaling pathways such as TLR4/NF-κB and the NLRP3 inflammasome. Targeted modulation of this axis shows potential in reducing seizure burden in experimental models, positioning it as an emerging target for therapy.
key_finding_ja: てんかん病態においてPIWI-piRNA軸はゲノム安定性の維持だけでなく、TLR4/NF-κBやNLRP3を介した神経炎症反応および神経興奮性を調節している。
why_it_matters_ja: PIWI-piRNA軸を標的とした介入は薬剤耐性てんかんの新たなバイオマーカーや治療戦略となる可能性があるが、送達技術や安全性に関する更なる検証が必要である。

title: Continuous theta burst stimulation delays L-DOPA-induced dyskinesia progression and ameliorates orolingual dyskinesia with concomitant reduction of striatal FosB/ΔFosB and neuroinflammation.
abstract: Chronic L-3,4-dihydroxyphenylalanine (L-DOPA) administration in patients with Parkinson's disease (PD) inevitably leads to L-DOPA-induced dyskinesia (LID), which can be more disabling than PD itself. Therefore, finding ways to prevent or delay LID progression is crucial. Continuous theta burst stimulation (cTBS), a patterned form of repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation, shows promise to alleviate LID. However, whether it can prevent or delay LID progression and the underlying mechanisms remain largely unknown. In this study, we administered L-DOPA daily with or without concurrent cTBS to hemiparkinsonian rats for 3 weeks. Electromagnetic simulation confirmed that the dorsolateral striatum is within the electromagnetic field generated by cTBS. Prolonged L-DOPA administration deteriorated LID progressively, whereas cTBS significantly delayed the development of axial, limb, and total dyskinesia, with orolingual dyskinesia even improving over time. Additionally, L-DOPA administration significantly increased the number of FosB/ΔFosB⁺ cells and CD68⁺/Iba1⁺ cells, with elevated iNOS, IL-1β, TNF-α, and IL-6 levels, without altering total microglial numbers in the dorsolateral striatum. cTBS reversed all these changes, reducing FosB/ΔFosB⁺ cells, CD68⁺/Iba1⁺ cells, and all 4 pro-inflammatory markers. Furthermore, FosB/ΔFosB⁺ cell numbers and pro-inflammatory marker levels positively correlated with the severity of total, axial, limb, and orolingual dyskinesia. Collectively, cTBS treatment delays the progression of LID and improves orolingual dyskinesia, which is closely associated with the reduction of FosB/∆FosB + cells and alleviation of microglia-related inflammation in the striatum.
authors: Wu X, Sun Q, Yang S, Wang Y, Bai Y, Hui Y, Li L, Qiao H, Zhang Q, Wang L.
screening_reason: The study directly measures and evaluates the reduction of striatal microglial activation and neuroinflammation following continuous theta burst stimulation.
summary_ja: ヘミパーキンソン病ラットモデルにおいて、L-DOPAの長期投与に持続的シータバースト刺激（cTBS）を併用する効果が検証された。L-DOPA単独投与はジスキネジアを進行させたが、cTBSの併用は軸性、四肢性、および総ジスキネジアの進行を遅らせ、口舌部ジスキネジアを改善した。また、cTBSは背外側線条体におけるFosB/ΔFosB陽性細胞数およびミクログリアに関連する炎症性マーカーの上昇を抑制した。これらの変化の抑制はジスキネジアの軽減と相関していた。
summary_en: In hemiparkinsonian rats, continuous theta burst stimulation (cTBS) combined with L-DOPA administration delayed the progression of axial, limb, and total dyskinesia while improving orolingual dyskinesia. Concurrently, cTBS reduced the accumulation of striatal FosB/ΔFosB-positive cells and suppressed microglial neuroinflammatory markers. These findings indicate that cTBS delays L-DOPA-induced dyskinesia progression in association with reduced striatal FosB/ΔFosB expression and neuroinflammation.
key_finding_ja: ヘミパーキンソン病ラットにおいて、cTBSの併用はL-DOPA誘発性ジスキネジアの進行を遅らせるとともに、線条体におけるFosB/ΔFosBの発現とミクログリア主導の神経炎症を抑制した。
why_it_matters_ja: L-DOPA誘発性ジスキネジアに対する神経刺激療法のメカニズムとして神経炎症の抑制が示唆され、新たな治療アプローチの開発に寄与する可能性がある。

title: Microglial immunometabolism in Alzheimer's disease: A stage-resolved trajectory from adaptive remodeling to the metabolic paradox.
abstract: Microglia are central regulators of the cellular phase of Alzheimer's disease (AD). Under chronic exposure to amyloid-β, pathological tau, and aging-associated bioenergetic decline, these cells undergo immunometabolic remodeling that may initially be adaptive. As stress persists, this remodeling can become maladaptive, marked by disordered glycolysis, disturbed lipid handling, mitochondrial dysfunction, and compensatory failure. In this review, we organize these changes as a stage-dependent trajectory from adaptive remodeling to functional decompensation. We introduce the "metabolic paradox" as an operational descriptor: a concurrent, same-cell mismatch between increased substrate uptake or inflammatory activation and declining bioenergetic efficiency and homeostatic function. Along this trajectory we examine neurovascular energy bottlenecks, substrate redistribution, triggering receptor expressed on myeloid cells 2 (TREM2)/apolipoprotein E (APOE)-dependent lipid homeostasis, mitochondrial and proteostatic collapse, and their links to persistent neuroinflammation, defective phagocytosis, aberrant synaptic pruning, and senescence-like dysfunction. We synthesize prior primary findings and stratify each major claim by evidentiary strength, avoiding the overinterpretation of model-specific results as patient-level mechanisms. Finally, we frame immunoprevention as mechanism-based, early-stage metabolic intervention to preserve homeostatic microglial function, a strategy whose clinical benefit remains a hypothesis requiring prospective testing.
authors: Zou Y, Ou Y, Zhao H, Chen G, Chen Z, Li Y, Jiang J.
screening_reason: The review focuses on microglial immunometabolism and its causal connection to persistent neuroinflammation in Alzheimer's disease.
summary_ja: アルツハイマー病（AD）におけるミクログリアの免疫代謝リモデリングについて、適応的変化から機能不全に至る病期依存的な軌跡を考察したレビューである。アミロイドβやタウ蛋白質の蓄積および加齢によるエネルギー代謝低下に対し、ミクログリアは初期には適応的に応答するが、持続的ストレスにより代謝不全が生じる。著者らは、基質取り込みや炎症活性化が増加しながらもエネルギー効率や恒常性維持が低下する現象を「代謝パラドックス」として概念化している。初期段階での代謝的介入による免疫予防可能性を提唱しているが、その臨床的有効性は今後の検証課題である。
summary_en: This review outlines a stage-dependent trajectory of microglial immunometabolic changes in Alzheimer's disease, progressing from adaptive remodeling to functional decompensation. It conceptualizes the "metabolic paradox," wherein microglia exhibit increased substrate uptake alongside impaired bioenergetic efficiency and homeostatic function. Early-stage metabolic interventions are proposed as a potential immunopreventive strategy to preserve homeostatic microglial function.
key_finding_ja: アルツハイマー病におけるミクログリアの免疫代謝変化は、初期の適応的応答から基質取り込みとエネルギー効率低下が同居する「代謝パラドックス」を経て機能障害へと進行する。
why_it_matters_ja: ミクログリアの代謝不全メカニズムの解明は、アルツハイマー病の発症初期における新たな免疫予防的治療法の開発につながる可能性がある。

title: Immunological drivers of oxidative stress in glaucoma: implications for antioxidant therapy.
abstract: Glaucoma is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by RGC loss and irreversible visual impairment, representing the second leading cause of global blindness. Immune-inflammatory responses and oxidative stress are core pathological drivers of glaucomatous optic nerve degeneration, forming a vicious cycle via the TLR4/NF-κB/NLRP3 inflammasome axis, complement overactivation, and dysregulation of the endogenous antioxidant system. These processes trigger sustained neuroinflammation, mitochondrial dysfunction, and RGC apoptosis. Antioxidant therapies targeting the immune-oxidative stress axis have emerged as promising neuroprotective strategies, including classic antioxidants, Nrf2 activators (e.g., NOB), nanocarrier-mediated targeted delivery systems, and PBM. This mini-review summarizes key molecular mechanisms linking immune activation and oxidative damage in glaucoma, reviews recent advances in the development of antioxidant therapeutics, and discusses current challenges and future directions for clinical translation.
authors: Lin B, Fan W, Li DK.
journal: Graefe's archive for clinical and experimental ophthalmology = Albrecht von Graefes Archiv fur klinische und experimentelle Ophthalmologie
screening_reason: Reviews the neuroimmunological pathways, immune-inflammatory responses, and neuroinflammation driving optic nerve degeneration in glaucoma.
summary_ja: 緑内障は網膜神経節細胞の脱落と不可逆的な視力障害を特徴とする進行性神経変性疾患です。本ミニレビューでは、TLR4/NF-κB/NLRP3インフラマソーム軸や補体過剰活性化を介した免疫炎症応答と酸化ストレスの悪循環機構が整理されています。さらに、Nrf2活性化剤やナノ粒子ドラッグデリバリーなどの抗酸化標的療法の進行状況と臨床応用に向けた課題が論じられています。
summary_en: Glaucoma is a neurodegenerative disorder characterized by retinal ganglion cell loss and visual impairment driven by neuroinflammation and oxidative stress. This review summarizes the molecular mechanisms linking immune-inflammatory activation and oxidative damage, such as the TLR4/NF-κB/NLRP3 axis. It also discusses novel therapeutic strategies targeting the immune-oxidative stress axis and key challenges for clinical translation.
key_finding_ja: 緑内障における神経変性は免疫応答と酸化ストレスの悪循環により増幅され、これを標的とした抗酸化療法が新しい神経保護戦略として期待される。
why_it_matters_ja: 本解説は前臨床試験や概念実証段階の知見を中心にまとめられており、実際の臨床治療に導入するにはさらなるヒトでの検証が必要です。

title: Discovery of Anti-Neuroinflammatory Compounds in Alzheimer's Disease: Current Trends and Future Perspectives.
abstract: Chronic neuroinflammation in response to abnormal protein aggregates has been implicated as a critical mechanism in several neurodegenerative diseases, and the modulation of signaling pathways associated with inflammation is being explored as a potential strategy for new therapeutics. In Alzheimer's disease (AD), the neuroinflammation hypothesis also starts to influence the landscape of drug discovery in place of the previously regarded amyloid hypothesis. As such, the objective of this review is to compile recent advanced in the discovery of anti-neuroinflammatory compounds developed through chemical synthesis and structural modification, providing an overview of current trends in drug discovery strategies and scaffold redesign for the development of the next-generation of anti-neuroinflammatory therapeutics. It was found that the compounds described in the publications could be categorized into four groups: modification of natural compounds, rational drug design, drug screening approaches, and drug repurposing. While the categorization seems to be similar to drug discoveries in other fields, with the modification of natural compounds accounting for most publications, specific observations could still be made. Namely, the growing interest in the multitarget-directed ligand approach reflects the increasing recognition of AD as a multifactorial disease. Despite this, further research is required to identify additional effective activities or the appropriate combinations besides anti-neuroinflammatory activity. Lastly, this review also gives brief overview regarding physicochemical properties of central nervous system-active agents, of which anti-neuroinflammatory compounds are parts of, and suggests the adoption of in silico prediction models as screening tools before the use of in vitro or in vivo models.
authors: Paelaong N, Sripha K, Boondam Y.
screening_reason: The review directly focuses on medicinal chemistry and drug discovery strategies targeting anti-neuroinflammatory mechanisms in Alzheimer's disease.
summary_ja: 本レビューは、アルツハイマー病（AD）治療における抗神経炎症化合物の創薬研究の現状と将来の展望をまとめたものである。文献で報告されている化合物は、天然物の構造修飾、合理的創薬デザイン、化合物スクリーニング、ドラッグリパーパシングの4つの領域に分類された。ADの多面的な病態に対応するため、マルチターゲット指向型リガンドへの関心が高まっていることが示された。また、中枢神経系作用薬としての物理化学的プロパティの評価や、スクリーニングツールとしてのin silico予測モデルの活用が提唱されている。
summary_en: This review summarizes recent trends and therapeutic strategies in discovering anti-neuroinflammatory compounds for Alzheimer's disease. The surveyed approaches were categorized into natural product modification, rational drug design, high-throughput screening, and drug repurposing. The authors highlight the potential of multitarget-directed ligands and advocate for integrating in silico prediction tools early in the drug discovery process.
key_finding_ja: アルツハイマー病に対する抗神経炎症化合物の創薬アプローチを4分類に整理し、マルチターゲット指向型設計やin silico予測モデルの導入が重要であることを提示した。
why_it_matters_ja: アルツハイマー病に対する神経炎症を標的とした新薬開発の方向性やスクリーニング手法の最適化に寄与する可能性がある。

title: Associations of self-reported and actigraphic sleep with gut microbiome composition and diversity among older adults.
abstract: Study objectives Poor sleep is linked to adverse health outcomes. Animal studies suggest the gut microbiome may influence sleep, but human findings remain inconsistent. We examined associations of self-reported insomnia symptoms, daytime sleepiness, and actigraphy-measured sleep with gut microbiome diversity and composition in older adults. Methods We studied 869 Baltimore Longitudinal Study of Aging participants with self-reported sleep and shotgun metagenomic sequencing; 332 also had actigraphy. We tested associations of sleep with alpha diversity, beta diversity, and species composition using regression, PERMANOVA, and ANCOM-BC2, adjusting for age, sex, BMI, physical activity, education, and depressive symptoms. Results Participants had mean age 70.7 years; 54.8% were female and 66.9% White. Trouble falling asleep ≥5 times/week was associated with higher Shannon diversity (β=0.41 SD; 95% CI: 0.09, 0.73) and Pielou's evenness, but not richness metrics. No actigraphy-measured sleep variables were associated with alpha or beta diversity. Beta diversity analyses suggested excessive sleepiness (1-2 o 3-4 times/week) was associated with different microbial composition, though variance explained was small. In species-level analyses, frequent insomnia symptoms or excessive sleepiness were associated with depleted or undetected Eubacterium sp. CAG:251. In exploratory actigraphy models, each doubling of sleep efficiency was associated with higher Eubacterium sp. CAG:251 prevalence (PR=2.15; 95% CI: 1.47, 3.14), while each 30-minute increase in wake after sleep onset was associated with lower prevalence (PR=0.49; 95% CI: 0.29, 0.81). Conclusions Global diversity findings were limited and inconsistent, whereas subjective and objective sleep disturbances converged on Eubacterium sp. CAG:251. Findings are exploratory and require longitudinal replication.
authors: Tilves C, Holingue C, Wanigatunga SK, Chia CW, Zhao N, Wu MN, Schrack JA, Simonsick EM, Ferrucci L, Tanaka T, Spira AP, Mueller NT.
screening_reason: The paper directly investigates the association between sleep parameters and gut microbiome diversity and species composition in older adults.
summary_ja: 高齢者869名を対象に、主観的評価およびアクチグラフィによる睡眠データと腸内細菌叢の関連を横断的に解析しました。全体の菌叢多様性との関連は限定的で一貫性を欠く一方、不眠症状や過度な昼間の眠気の双方が特定腸内細菌Eubacterium sp. CAG:251の検出低下と関連していました。さらに探索的な解析では、アクチグラフィで測定した睡眠効率の高さが本菌種の存在確率の上昇と関連していました。
summary_en: This study examined associations between self-reported or actigraphy-measured sleep parameters and gut microbiome characteristics in 869 older adults. While overall diversity findings were limited, both subjective and objective measures of sleep disturbance consistently converged on lower relative abundance or prevalence of Eubacterium sp. CAG:251. Higher sleep efficiency was linked to increased prevalence of this specific bacterial species.
key_finding_ja: 高齢者において、主観的および客観的な睡眠障害指標が特定腸内細菌Eubacterium sp. CAG:251の減少と一貫して関連していた。
why_it_matters_ja: 睡眠障害と特定の腸内細菌種との関連を示した本結果は、今後の縦断的研究を通じた腸脳相関の解明に寄与することが期待されます。
